commits.pr_title: [Model] Add masked_token_ids to never sample given tokens
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Some token ids must never be sampled: the `lm_head` rows past the tokenizer (padding, so the logits exist but decode to nothing; see #13175) and, for multimodal models, placeholder tokens that are meaningless without their media. Today the only options are per-request `allowed_token_ids` (very slow with a large allow-list) or patching `compute_logits`, which RL frameworks do (e.g. verl, [`monkey_patch_compute_logits`](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/453954b3/verl/workers/rollout/vllm_rollout/utils.py#L117-L145), added in verl-project/verl#7038). RL makes this worse than plain inference: training perturbs the untrained rows and a sampled OOV token feeds back into the policy.

This adds an engine-level `--masked-token-ids` (`ModelConfig.masked_token_ids`):

- The model runner (`GPUModelRunner.sample()` and the standalone CPU runner) sets those logits to `-inf` once, on the full-vocab target logits, after the batch-sharded all-to-all and before the grammar bitmask and the sampler. Draft heads with their own vocab and TP-sharded logits are not touched.
- Draft tokens that hit a masked id are always rejected by the lossless rejection samplers, since the target gives them probability 0. The lossy methods (`synthetic`, `fly`) can accept draft tokens regardless of the target logits, so they are rejected at config time.
- The ids are validated against the vocab size at startup.
- Prompt logprobs are unaffected.

This is the "add the masking to the sampler" direction suggested in #13175 (njhill, Dec 2025). Defaulting to masking everything past the tokenizer could be a follow-up. The runner-side design is from @njhill's review.

Tracking: #68777.

## Test Plan / Result

`tests/v1/sample/test_masked_token_ids.py`: masking all but one token makes it the only sample (greedy and seeded random), out-of-range ids fail at config time, lossy rejection methods are rejected. All 5 pass on GB200 (nightly 8586ccbc + this branch).

Earlier version (mask in `LogitsProcessor`): Qwen3-0.6B / Qwen3-4B-FP8 / Qwen3-30B-A3B with `masked_token_ids` = lm_head rows past the tokenizer: GSM8K unchanged (GB200).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Return 400 for unreadable embedding payloads
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Return HTTP 400 for unreadable `prompt_embeds`, `image_embeds`,
`audio_embeds`, and `video_embeds` payloads instead of leaking deserialization
failures as HTTP 500. Closes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/69063.

## Claims

- Converts malformed client embedding payloads to parameter-specific
  `VLLMValidationError` responses.
- Preserves host and device OOM failures as server errors.
- Reuses one thread-safe loader for all embedding types and always maps
  client-controlled tensor storage to CPU.
- Adds unit and OpenAI server regression coverage and documents the behavior.

## Validation

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/renderers \
  tests/renderers/test_prompt_embeds_payload_validation.py \
  tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_validation.py \
  tests/renderers/test_sparse_tensor_concurrent_race.py \
  -q -k 'not prompt_embeds_input_width'
```

```text
104 passed, 4 deselected, 21 warnings in 6.04s
```

`git diff --check`, Python compilation, and the docstring style checker also
passed. The LLaVA 7B `RemoteOpenAIServer` regression test was not run locally
because the required model-serving environment was unavailable.

## Details

`torch.load` raises several non-`ValueError` exception types for malformed
payloads, so the generic API exception handler treated client input errors as
HTTP 500. The new shared loader catches deserialization failures, bounds the
reflected error text, and raises `VLLMValidationError` with the affected request
parameter. Memory exhaustion is deliberately re-raised, since it may indicate
server capacity rather than invalid input.

All client embedding archives are loaded on CPU so checkpoint device metadata
cannot select server device allocations. Existing archive-size, sparse-tensor,
and densification protections remain in the shared path.

Duplicate-work checks were exec, no duplicate work:

```bash
gh issue view 69063 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "69063 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open \
  --search "unreadable embedding payload 400"
```

```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Security] Complete input-bound hardening left incomplete by PR #51447
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

PR #51447 ("Bound generation inputs before expensive work") introduced bounds for five request parameters but left residual gaps in each. This PR closes all four gaps with one commit per issue, applying defense-in-depth at the Pydantic request model, `SamplingParams.__post_init__`, and frontend validation layers.

The four problems and their fixes:

| Commit | Gap in PR #51447 | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ee0be1c` | `stop_token_ids`: `dict.fromkeys` dedup removed duplicates but no count cap on distinct IDs, no Pydantic-layer bound, and `check_stop` used O(n) list scan per token | Add `VLLM_MAX_STOP_TOKEN_IDS` (default 128) enforced at Pydantic (`StopTokenIdsParam`), `SamplingParams.__post_init__`, and `frozenset` for O(1) lookup in `check_stop` |
| `b940cf6` | `stop` strings: `StopParam` only covered 4 OpenAI request models; `/inference/v1/generate` passes raw `SamplingParams` with no bound; `__post_init__` neither deduped nor capped `stop` | Add `dict.fromkeys` dedup and `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS` count cap in `__post_init__`, protecting every entry path |
| `d0cc00c` | DeepSeek V3.2 chat encoder: `find_last_user_index` was hoisted (1 of 2 quadratic scans removed), but the `role=="tool"` backwards scan remained O(k^2) for k consecutive tool messages | Thread `last_assistant_idx` through `encode_messages`/`render_message` for O(1) tool-result lookup; make `last_user_idx` required to prevent silent regression |
| `cce65fc` | `bad_words`: no Pydantic `max_length` (150k entries pass validation, waste prompt rendering before cap fires); `VLLM_MAX_BAD_WORDS_TOTAL_TOKENS` only enforced in GPU worker as bare `ValueError` | Add `BadWordsParam` Pydantic type, count cap in `__post_init__`, and total-token enforcement in `update_from_tokenizer` as `VLLMValidationError` |

## Why it matters

An unauthenticated client (on default `vllm serve` without `--api-key`) could exploit any of these gaps to force disproportionate CPU or scheduler work with a single request, degrading service availability for all concurrent users. These paths do not expose data or execute code; their impact is reduced service availability.

## How it was tested

Merged current upstream `main` and documented the request limits. `pytest tests/test_request_input_bounds.py tests/test_sampling_params.py` passed 159 tests on macOS. OpenAI Codex assisted with the branch update and validation.

13 new regression tests added to `tests/test_request_input_bounds.py`, covering all four fixes. Full suite (35 tests) passes:

```
tests/test_request_input_bounds.py    35 passed in 4.74s
```

Tests exercise:
- `stop_token_ids` count cap at SamplingParams and Pydantic layers, frozenset property
- `stop` string dedup and count cap at SamplingParams level
- DeepSeek V3.2 tool-message linear-time assertion (counting list reads)
- `bad_words` Pydantic cap, SamplingParams count cap, total-token limit enforcement

## Reference

- Original fix: PR #51447
- Advisory: GHSA-4c3x-h2r4-j55f (original)
- Gaps reported by: axel-mierczuk-1pw (Axel Mierczuk @ 1Password)
  - GHSA-cg76-73hw-qg4m (stop_token_ids)
  - GHSA-v782-f4x3-chvf (stop strings)
  - GHSA-4r96-ccfx-mq85 (DeepSeek quadratic scan)
  - GHSA-9862-57p7-p868 (bad_words)

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Model] Export ZAYA1 CCA prefill checkpoints
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Let ZAYA1's CCA layer export align-mode prefill checkpoints. With prefix caching on, the scheduler stops splitting a prompt at its last Mamba block boundary only if every Mamba layer can export a checkpoint. CCA declared none, so every long ZAYA1 prompt took an extra prefill step.

Follow-up to #68673, which added checkpoints to the ShortConv metadata builder that CCA already uses. No open PR covers ZAYA1.

## Claims

- In align mode, `ZayaCCA` declares checkpoint alignment 1. Its state is the last `cca_time0 + cca_time1 - 2` raw q/k inputs plus the previous token's delayed value, so at each checkpoint offset it copies those inputs into the checkpoint block. It does this in PyTorch, like the rest of the layer, without a host sync.
- Rows without a checkpoint write the null block, as the layer's graph-padding rows already do.
- ZAYA1-8B, ISL 8000: a cold prompt now prefills in one step (8000) instead of two (7936 + 64). Mean TTFT drops 15-38% on B300 and 18-33% on MI355X (C1/C4/C8).
- Cost: one checkpoint block per request reserves 0.386% of KV-cache token capacity. Activation and CUDA graph memory are unchanged.

## Validation

Base is the merge-base d9d7e9434f; PR is fa4434673f. Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B@67d34da515, TP1, 64-token blocks, prefix caching on. B300 and MI355X, both arms with the same environment. On MI355X both arms set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR=0` (the AITER linear path fails on one-dimensional inputs on main too) and use `TRITON_ATTN`.

### Tests

`test_zaya_cca_exports_state_at_checkpoint` runs `ZayaCCA._mix_with_state` on a decode and two prefills that checkpoint mid-query. Each checkpoint block must equal the state of the same prefill stopped at its offset, and nothing else in the cache may change.

```bash
pytest "tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py::test_zaya_cca_exports_state_at_checkpoint" \
       "tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py::test_zaya_cca_state"
```

| | B300 | MI355X | CPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_zaya_cca_exports_state_at_checkpoint`, PR | pass | pass | pass |
| same, export disabled | fail (checkpoint mismatch) | fail (checkpoint mismatch) | fail (24/24 elements) |
| `test_zaya_cca_state` (HF vs vLLM, APC), base and PR | pass | pass | |

`test_zaya_cca_state` also passes on base, so it does not show that the export runs; the direct test is the regression guard. CI runs both in `language-models-tests-hybrid`.

### Prefill steps on real weights

An 8000-token prompt, then a follow-up sharing its first 7936 tokens, then a cache reset and the prompt again:

| | cold | follow-up | after reset |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | 7936 + 64 | 64 computed, 7936 hit | 7936 + 64 |
| PR | 8000 | 64 computed, 7936 hit | 8000 |

Generated tokens match within each arm and between base and PR. Max chosen-token logprob difference, base vs PR: B300 0.047 cold / 0.004 cached; MI355X 0.046 cold / 0.089 cached.

### TTFT

`vllm serve Zyphra/ZAYA1-8B` with prefix caching, `vllm bench serve` random dataset, ISL 8000 / OSL 32, 16 fresh prompts per point. A throwaway round, then Base1 / PR1 / PR2 / Base2 on an exclusive node. All 16/16 requests completed in every round. Mean TTFT (ms):

| GPU | Conc. | Base1 | Base2 | PR1 | PR2 | Base mean | PR mean | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300 | 1 | 139.56 | 137.19 | 86.77 | 84.07 | 138.37 | 85.42 | -38.3% |
| B300 | 4 | 290.02 | 284.82 | 245.91 | 241.50 | 287.42 | 243.70 | -15.2% |
| B300 | 8 | 422.44 | 415.00 | 353.95 | 356.85 | 418.72 | 355.40 | -15.1% |
| MI355X | 1 | 164.19 | 168.90 | 111.00 | 113.70 | 166.54 | 112.35 | -32.5% |
| MI355X | 4 | 393.83 | 400.65 | 312.70 | 309.42 | 397.24 | 311.06 | -21.7% |
| MI355X | 8 | 596.66 | 581.00 | 473.14 | 488.87 | 588.83 | 481.00 | -18.3% |

KV-cache tokens: B300 2,267,850 → 2,259,094; MI355X 2,475,127 → 2,465,570 (both -0.386%). Available KV memory, peak activation, CUDA graph memory and graph counts are identical between arms.

### Accuracy

Full GSM8K (1319 questions), 5-shot raw completions (the checkpoint has no chat template), temperature 0, seed 42, max 256 tokens, concurrency 8, two server launches per arm. Every run had 846,720 prefix-cache-hit tokens, so checkpoint reuse is heavily exercised. Raw accuracy is a lower bound: this model often emits EOS immediately.

| GPU | Base correct (r1 / r2) | PR correct (r1 / r2) | Base mean | PR mean | Base answered-only | PR answered-only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300 | 427 / 415 | 410 / 422 | 31.92% | 31.54% | 51.78% | 51.90% |
| MI355X | 522 / 503 | 521 / 498 | 38.86% | 38.63% | 55.69% | 54.34% |

Differences are within launch noise: on B300 matched rounds change sign (-17, +7), and on MI355X the per-question Base-only / PR-only correct counts are 134 / 133 and 140 / 135.

## Details

- A checkpoint lies at least one prefix-cache block into its prefill, which is longer than the q/k history (2 tokens for ZAYA1-8B), so the history is all prefill tokens (asserted).
- Not covered: TP/DP/EP, PD disaggregation and other block sizes.
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the implementation; validation runs were reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Keep marker token embeddings for pruned Qwen3-VL video on encoder-only instances
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

An encoder-only instance (`--mm-encoder-only`, or an `ec_producer`) crashes at startup with Qwen3-VL when `--video-pruning-rate` is set. This keeps the token embedding table loaded on such an instance so pruned video outputs can be built.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs and issues for `mm-encoder-only pruning`, `encoder-only video pruning Qwen3-VL`, `ec_producer video_pruning_rate` and `encoder output width pruning` and found nothing covering this. #54208 / #54170 are a different failure (Qwen3.5 missing `video_pruning_method`).

## Claims

- A Qwen3-VL EC producer with video pruning enabled starts instead of crashing in the startup encoder-width measurement.
- An encoder-only instance produces the same pruned video embeddings as a full instance.

## Validation

Hardware: 1x RTX 6000 Ada (48 GB). Model: `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`. Base: `a2915755bf`.

Reproducer (same command on both):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct --max-model-len 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.2 --video-pruning-rate 0.5 \
  --ec-transfer-config '{"ec_connector":"ECExampleConnector","ec_role":"ec_producer","ec_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"/tmp/ec"}}'
```

Main (`a2915755bf`):

```text
File "vllm/distributed/ec_transfer/ec_connector/encoder_output_width.py", line 53, in _measure_on_worker
    outputs = model.embed_multimodal(**mm_kwargs)
File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py", line 2978, in embed_multimodal
File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_vl.py", line 2506, in _postprocess_video_embeds_evs
...
NotImplementedError: The register_meta function for torch.nonzero() raises unimplemented by default, as a correct data-independent implementation does not exist. ...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

This PR:

```text
INFO [encoder_output_width.py:83] EC producer encoder output widths: {'image': 8197, 'video': 8197}
```

and `/health` returns 200.

New regression test, comparing the pruned video embedding of an encoder-only instance with a full instance:

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_qwen3_vl.py -q
```

- Main: `1 failed` with `Call to collective_rpc method failed: The register_meta function for torch.nonzero() raises unimplemented by default ...`
- This PR: `1 passed in 43.44s`

New weight-mapping test, checking that the token embedding is routed to the kept table for each checkpoint layout that shares this code (Qwen3-VL, Cosmos3, Alpamayo2 Super, three ColQwen3 layouts) and that other language-model weights are not rerouted:

```bash
pytest tests/models/multimodal/test_mapping.py -k marker_embed -q
```

- This PR: `6 passed`
- With a redirect keyed on Qwen3-VL's checkpoint name only (the first revision of this PR), the Cosmos3, Alpamayo2 Super and ColQwen3 `vlm.` layouts resolve to `language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight`, leaving the kept table without weights.

Also checked on a multi-shard checkpoint (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, 4 shards) with the same command: the producer starts (`EC producer encoder output widths: {'image': 16389, 'video': 16389}`), and the loader skips 2 of 4 language-model shards instead of 3, because the shard holding `embed_tokens` is kept.

Also ran the regression test against a compressed-tensors FP8 Qwen3-VL-8B checkpoint (local, `Linear` targets only, embedding left in BF16): it passes. This shows a quantized checkpoint still loads, but it does not exercise an embedding quantized by layer path.

`pre-commit` passes on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** With pruning enabled, `_create_final_video_embeddings` builds the full replacement segment for a video: the retained video tokens interleaved with the text embeddings of the timestamp and vision marker tokens. Those come from `get_language_model().embed_input_ids(...)`. Under `--mm-encoder-only` the language model is a `StageMissingLayer` wrapping modules built on the `meta` device, so the lookup returns meta tensors, and the position bookkeeping that follows fails on boolean indexing. An EC producer hits this at startup because `measure_encoder_output_widths` encodes a dummy video.

**Fix.** When the instance is encoder-only and pruning is enabled, Qwen3-VL keeps a `VocabParallelEmbedding` (`marker_embed_tokens`) outside the language model and uses it for that lookup. The instance-level `hf_to_vllm_mapper` gets one extra rule, applied after the model's existing ones, that routes the mapped name `language_model.model.embed_tokens.` to it. Matching the mapped name keeps this independent of the checkpoint layout, so subclasses with their own mappers are covered, and it also makes the encoder-only shard filter keep the shard that holds the table. The table is created with the layer path the language model gives its own embedding, so a quantization scheme that targets the embedding by path still applies. Nothing changes for full instances or for encoder-only instances without pruning.

**Tradeoffs and limits.**

- The encoder-only instance now holds the embedding table (vocab x hidden size, about 0.6 GB for 2B and 1.2 GB for 8B in bf16) and may read one more shard.
- `Qwen3VLMoeForConditionalGeneration` gets the same call but I did not test it. For Cosmos3, Alpamayo2 Super and ColQwen3, which inherit the Qwen3-VL `__init__`, only the weight-name mapping is tested; I did not run their checkpoints as encoder-only instances.
- No test covers an embedding quantized by layer path; I do not have such a checkpoint.
- Other subclasses with their own `__init__` (Qwen3.5, InternS1-Pro) are unchanged. Qwen3.5 inherits the same code path and will likely need the same call, but with pruning it currently fails earlier for an unrelated reason (#54170, #54208), so I could not test it here.
- The new generation test is added to the "Multimodal Models (Standard) 2: qwen3 + gemma" CI step; the mapping test is in `test_mapping.py`, which CI already runs.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel][GDN] Faster fused CUDA MTP decode for 16-bit recurrent state
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Add a separate fused GDN MTP decode kernel for 16-bit (BF16/FP16) recurrent state, and let the fused CUDA path take FP16 state (`--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16` falls back to Triton on `main`). At 16 bits the existing kernel is bound by the warp-shuffle reductions, not state traffic: **1.3–1.6×** faster kernel, **up to 5.3%** faster decode steps on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8. The kernel design is adapted from FlashInfer's `cake_gdn` BF16-state MTP decode kernel by @yyihuang, added in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4581 (Apache-2.0, shipped in v0.7.3); credit for the layout goes there. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used.

## Claims

- 16-bit state reaches 5.8–6.3 TB/s at 32+ requests (from ~4.0), on par with FP32 state. FP32 state and small batches (V split) still run the existing kernel, unchanged.
- **Bitwise-identical** outputs and state to the existing kernel; GSM8K unchanged.
- FP16 state now runs the fused CUDA kernel. The ROCm AITER decode gate keeps its own FP32/BF16 list, since AITER rejects FP16 state.

## Validation

```bash

```python
"""Decode-only load for hybrid (GDN) models: a long cached prefix, then decode.

GDN layers keep a recurrent state only at block boundaries, mainly at a
prompt's replay boundary (length - 1, rounded down to a block), so a request
hits its prefix only if an earlier prompt ended just past it. The driver:

1. warm:    the first prefix-len + 1 tokens of each prompt, 1 output token.
2. probe:   the warm prompts again; every request must hit its full prefix.
3. measure: prefix + fresh tokens, `--output-len` tokens each, all requests
            at once, repeated `--rounds` times with the same prompts.

Greedy sampling, so arms with bitwise-identical kernels see the same tokens
and the same MTP acceptance. Request i goes to DP rank i % dp-size. Serve with
--enable-prompt-tokens-details so responses report cached_tokens.
"""

import argparse
import asyncio
import json
import random
import statistics
import time

import aiohttp

TOKEN_RANGE = (1000, 150_000)  # ordinary vocabulary, clear of special tokens
ACCEPTANCE_METRICS = (
    "vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_total",
    "vllm:spec_decode_num_drafts_total",
)

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
parser.add_argument("--base-url", required=True)
parser.add_argument("--model", required=True)
parser.add_argument("--prefix-len", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--fresh-len", type=int, default=1)
parser.add_argument("--output-len", type=int, default=1024)
parser.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--rounds", type=int, default=5)
parser.add_argument("--dp-size", type=int, default=1)
parser.add_argument("--block-size", type=int, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
parser.add_argument("--result", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
assert args.concurrency % args.dp_size == 0, "give every DP rank equal requests"
assert args.prefix_len % args.block_size == 0, "a hit lands on a block boundary"

rng = random.Random(args.seed)
prompt_len = args.prefix_len + args.fresh_len
prompts = [rng.choices(range(*TOKEN_RANGE), k=prompt_len) for _ in range(args.concurrency)]
warm_prompts = [p[: args.prefix_len + 1] for p in prompts]


async def complete(session, i, prompt, max_tokens):
    body = {
        "model": args.model, "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": max_tokens,
        "ignore_eos": True, "temperature": 0.0, "stream": True,
        "stream_options": {"include_usage": True},
    }
    headers = {"X-data-parallel-rank": str(i % args.dp_size)}
    start = time.perf_counter()
    first = last = usage = None
    async with session.post(f"{args.base_url}/v1/completions", json=body,
                            headers=headers) as resp:
        if resp.status != 200:
            raise RuntimeError(f"request {i}: HTTP {resp.status}: {await resp.text()}")
        while line := await resp.content.readline(max_line_length=2**28):
            if not line.startswith(b"data: ") or line.startswith(b"data: [DONE]"):
                continue
            chunk = json.loads(line[6:])
            if "error" in chunk:
                raise RuntimeError(f"request {i}: {chunk['error']}")
            if chunk.get("choices"):
                last = time.perf_counter()
                first = first or last
            usage = chunk.get("usage") or usage
    out = usage["completion_tokens"]
    return {
        "cached": usage["prompt_tokens_details"]["cached_tokens"],
        "ttft_ms": (first - start) * 1e3,
        "tpot_ms": (last - first) * 1e3 / (out - 1) if out > 1 else None,
    }


async def phase(session, name, batch, max_tokens):
    start = time.perf_counter()
    results = await asyncio.gather(
        *(complete(session, i, p, max_tokens) for i, p in enumerate(batch)))
    print(f"{name}: {len(results)} requests in {time.perf_counter() - start:.1f} s")
    return results


def check_hits(name, results, length):
    expected = min(args.prefix_len, length - 1) // args.block_size * args.block_size
    cached = [r["cached"] for r in results]
    print(f"{name}: cached tokens {min(cached)}-{max(cached)}, expected {expected}")
    if min(cached) < expected:
        raise SystemExit(f"{name}: some requests missed their cached prefix")


async def acceptance(session):
    async with session.get(f"{args.base_url}/metrics") as resp:
        text = await resp.text()
    totals = {}
    for line in text.splitlines():
        name = line.split("{")[0].split(" ")[0]
        if name in ACCEPTANCE_METRICS:
            totals[name] = totals.get(name, 0.0) + float(line.rsplit(" ", 1)[1])
    return totals


async def main():
    connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=0, force_close=True)
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession(
        connector=connector, timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=None)
    ) as session:
        await phase(session, "warm", warm_prompts, 1)
        check_hits("probe", await phase(session, "probe", warm_prompts, 1),
                   len(warm_prompts[0]))
        rounds = []
        for r in range(args.rounds):
            before = await acceptance(session)
            results = await phase(session, f"measure {r}", prompts, args.output_len)
            after = await acceptance(session)
            check_hits(f"measure {r}", results, prompt_len)
            drafts = after[ACCEPTANCE_METRICS[1]] - before[ACCEPTANCE_METRICS[1]]
            accepted = after[ACCEPTANCE_METRICS[0]] - before[ACCEPTANCE_METRICS[0]]
            rounds.append({
                "tpot_ms_mean": statistics.mean(x["tpot_ms"] for x in results),
                "acceptance_length": 1 + accepted / drafts,
            })
            print(rounds[-1], flush=True)
    summary = {
        "args": vars(args),
        "tpot_ms_median": statistics.median(x["tpot_ms_mean"] for x in rounds),
        "acceptance_length": statistics.median(x["acceptance_length"] for x in rounds),
        "rounds": rounds,
    }
    with open(args.result, "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=2)
    print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != "args"}, indent=2))


asyncio.run(main())
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>Kernel benchmark and bitwise dump</summary>

```python
"""Fused GDN MTP decode: kernel time and bitwise dump, run once per venv.

  python bench_gdn_mtp.py bench <out.csv>   # CUPTI, CUDA graph, cold L2
  python bench_gdn_mtp.py dump <out.pt>     # outputs + state for a bitwise A/B

Shapes are Qwen3.8-Flash-Next per GPU under DP/EP (H=16, HV=48, K=V=128).
"""

import sys

import pandas as pd
import torch
from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti

import vllm._C_stable_libtorch  # noqa: F401  registers torch.ops._C

K = V = 128
SCALE = K**-0.5
EPS = 1e-6


def make_inputs(H, HV, query_lengths, state_dtype, seed=0, state_scale=0.05):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    dev = "cuda"
    num_reqs = len(query_lengths)
    width = max(query_lengths)
    L = sum(query_lengths)
    num_slots = num_reqs * width + 1
    mixed_qkv = torch.randn(L, 2 * H * K + HV * V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    a = torch.randn(L, HV, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    b = torch.randn(L, HV, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    A_log = 0.5 * torch.randn(HV, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    dt_bias = 0.1 * torch.randn(HV, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    output_gate = torch.randn(L, HV, V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    norm_weight = torch.randn(V, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)
    state = (state_scale * torch.randn(num_slots, HV, V, K, device=dev)).to(state_dtype)
    # Request r reads slot r*width+1 (accepted = 1) and writes one snapshot
    # per token into its own slots; slot 0 is the null slot.
    state_indices = torch.arange(1, num_slots, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev).view(
        num_reqs, width
    )
    cu = [0]
    for q in query_lengths:
        cu.append(cu[-1] + q)
    cu_seqlens = torch.tensor(cu, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    num_accepted = torch.ones(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
    out = torch.empty(L, HV, V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=dev)
    return [mixed_qkv, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, state_indices, cu_seqlens,
            num_accepted, state, output_gate, norm_weight, out]


def run(args, gate="silu"):
    torch.ops._C.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp(*args, SCALE, EPS, gate)


def bench(path):
    H, HV = 16, 48
    rows = []
    for T in (4, 8):  # MTP3, MTP7
        for num_reqs in (4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128):
            for state_dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
                args = make_inputs(H, HV, (T,) * num_reqs, state_dtype)
                run(args)
                times = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
                    lambda: run(args), use_cuda_graph=True, cold_l2_cache=True,
                    dry_run_iters=20, repeat_iters=200,
                )
                us = 1e3 * float(torch.tensor(times).median())
                # State traffic: one read plus T snapshot writes per request.
                state_bytes = num_reqs * HV * V * K * state_dtype.itemsize * (1 + T)
                rows.append(dict(T=T, num_reqs=num_reqs,
                                 state=str(state_dtype).split(".")[-1],
                                 us=us, tbps=state_bytes / us / 1e6))
                print(rows[-1], flush=True)
    pd.DataFrame(rows).to_csv(path, index=False)


def dump(path):
    # Ragged lengths, skipped slots, accepted > 1, head ratios, both gates,
    # tiny (FP32-denormal-range) state; small and large batches cover both the
    # V-split and the non-split paths.
    cases = []
    for HV_per_H in (1, 2, 3, 4, 8):
        for lengths in ((4,) * 16, (9, 9, 4, 2, 1, 0) * 4, (2,) * 64, (4, 4)):
            for state_dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
                for gate in ("silu", "sigmoid"):
                    for state_scale in (0.05, 1e-39):
                        cases.append((HV_per_H, lengths, state_dtype, gate, state_scale))
    results = {}
    for i, (ratio, lengths, state_dtype, gate, state_scale) in enumerate(cases):
        H = 16 if ratio < 8 else 4
        args = make_inputs(H, ratio * H, lengths, state_dtype, seed=i,
                           state_scale=state_scale)
        width = max(lengths)
        acc = torch.tensor([min(1 + (r % 3), max(width, 1)) for r in range(len(lengths))],
                           dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
        args[7] = acc
        # Drop some destination slots (-1 / 0 means "don't write").
        args[5][::5, -1] = 0
        run(args, gate)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        results[i] = dict(out=args[11].cpu(), state=args[8].cpu(),
                          case=(ratio, lengths, str(state_dtype), gate, state_scale))
    torch.save(results, path)
    print(f"dumped {len(results)} cases to {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    {"bench": bench, "dump": dump}[sys.argv[1]](sys.argv[2])
```

## Details

- `fused_gdn_decode_16bit_kernel.cu` (new): 16-lane groups, each lane owns 8 contiguous K values of 4 rows. State moves as 128-bit loads/stores between global memory and registers, each dot product is a 9-shuffle reduce-scatter over 16 lanes (vs 20 over 32), q/k sit in padded shared memory, and SM10x uses packed FP32 math. 64 registers, 4 CTAs/SM.
- Attribution: from flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4581 (`cake_gdn_decode_pretranspose_mtp_t4_bf16state_wide128`): the 16-lane layout, 128-bit register-direct state access, padded q/k shared memory and packed f32x2 math. Our own: the reduce-scatter (it keeps the existing kernel's summation order), the gating/RMSNorm epilogue (copied from the existing kernel) and the vLLM op interface. The source file header cites the PR.
- Bitwise identity: a lane's two 4-value K halves are the partials of the old lanes 2m and 2m+1, reduced in the old butterfly order and added last. It holds against the existing kernel's unsplit path, the only case the new kernel replaces.
- `fused_gdn_decode_kernel.cu` launches the new kernel for 16-bit state when `choose_split_v` picks 1 (4+ requests at HV=48 on GB300). Shared constants move to `fused_gdn_decode.h`.
- Built for sm_103a only.

## Summary

- **Fix authentication bypass** in `AuthenticationMiddleware` when `--root-path` is set to a value that is a non-segment string prefix of a guarded route (e.g. `--root-path /v` against `/v1/models`).
- Replace `str.removeprefix(root_path)` with Starlette's `get_route_path(scope)`, which only strips `root_path` on a path-segment boundary — matching the same logic Starlette's router uses for dispatch.
- Add 9 regression tests covering non-segment-prefix bypass, legitimate segment-boundary stripping, and unguarded route accessibility.

## Details

`AuthenticationMiddleware` stripped `root_path` using `str.removeprefix`, a pure string operation with no path-segment awareness. Starlette's own route dispatcher (`get_route_path`) only strips `root_path` when it falls on a segment boundary (i.e. the path equals `root_path` exactly or `root_path` is followed by `/`). This mismatch meant:

- **Auth middleware**: `"/v1/models".removeprefix("/v")` → `"1/models"` → does not start with `/v1` → auth skipped
- **Starlette routing**: path still matches `/v1/models` → request dispatched normally

Result: complete bypass of `--api-key` bearer-token authentication on all guarded route families (`/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, `/cohere`) whenever `--root-path` happens to be a non-segment prefix.

- [x] All 20 existing auth middleware tests pass
- [x] 6 new parametrized tests for non-segment-prefix bypass (`/v` vs `/v1`, `/in` vs `/inference`, `/co` vs `/cohere`, `/` vs `/v1`)
- [x] 2 new tests for legitimate segment-boundary `root_path` values (`/api`, `/proxy`)

commits.pr_title: [Security] Widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32`
- Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension
- Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels

## Affected kernels

| Kernel | File | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC |
| `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path |
| `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High |
| `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate |
| AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) |

## Root cause

CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens.

## Fix pattern

```cpp
// Before (32-bit overflow)
scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size;

// After (64-bit safe)
const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x;
scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size;
```

For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change.

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing LayerNorm kernel tests pass
- [ ] Existing MoE kernel tests pass
- [ ] CI build succeeds on CUDA targets

This needs no weights. On base, every non-RGB mode fails on five of the six models: | Model | Base error for `L` / `LA` / `RGBA` / `P` frames | |---|---| | Qwen3-VL-4B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B | `L`, `P`: ``ImportError: `torchcodec` is not installed or can't be loaded``
`LA`, `RGBA`: `ValueError: Unable to infer channel dimension format` | | InternVL3-1B | `ValueError: Invalid mode for data type` | | LLaVA-OneVision-0.5B | `ValueError: Unable to infer channel dimension format` | | Ovis2.5-2B | no error (see Details) | With the PR, none of them fail. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Size rope_2d DP vision outputs from the spatial grid
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--mm-encoder-tp-mode data`, Kimi-K2.5/K2.6 video chunks get the wrong number of vision embeddings. The data-parallel path assumes every frame produces its own embeddings, but Kimi's vision encoder (`rope_2d`) averages a chunk's frames together. So a t-frame chunk is handed t times too many rows: its neighbours' embeddings plus padding.

**Fix:** for `rope_2d` encoders, size each item's output from its height x width only. Other encoders are unchanged.

(#65352 edits the same function but fixes a different bug.)

## Claims

- Kimi video chunks get the right number of embeddings, e.g. 252 instead of 1008 for a 4-frame 336x588 chunk.
- Images in the same batch are also fixed: the wrong counts shifted every later item's slice (max difference 1.73 vs the non-DP path).
- No change for other encoders (`mrope`, e.g. Qwen-VL).

## Validation

Unit tests in `tests/models/test_vision.py` compare the data-parallel output with running the model directly, for one image and three video chunks. The single-process test runs in the CPU "Basic Models Other" step; the 2-GPU test in the multi-GPU step.

```
pytest tests/models/test_vision.py -k rope_2d_temporal_pooling     # 2x H100
  main (a3b845e2):  2 failed   E  assert [4, 24, 12, 12] == [4, 6, 6, 4]
  this PR:          2 passed, 1 warning in 17.41s

pytest tests/models/test_vision.py                                 # this PR, 2x H100
  20 passed, 1 skipped, 8 warnings in 128.81s   (skip: needs 4 GPUs)
```

Real Kimi-K2.6 weights on 1x B300, data-parallel path vs normal path:

| | embeddings per item | vs normal path |
|---|---|---|
| expected | [448, 252, 112, 448] | |
| main | [448, 1008, 224, 1792] | wrong |
| this PR | [448, 252, 112, 448] | equal |

## Details

**Root cause:** the function sized each GPU's output as (input patches) / (spatial merge factor). That is right for `mrope` encoders, but `rope_2d` encoders also average the frames, so each item yields h * w / factor embeddings. The fix computes each item's output size once and uses it for padding, slicing and reordering, as the encoder CUDA-graph path already does. It uses only host-side sizes, so there is no added CPU/GPU sync.

**Not a duplicate:** the open PRs touching this function (#65352, #53164, #55587) fix other bugs; none change output sizing.

If #68737 lands first, this needs a trivial rebase: both add a test and an import to `tests/models/test_vision.py`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Multimodal] Encoder CUDA graphs for the Qwen3-Omni / Qwen3-ASR audio tower
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add encoder CUDA graph support to the Qwen3-Omni audio tower, which Qwen3-ASR also uses. The existing `cudagraph_mm_encoder` flag now covers audio through `SupportsEncoderCudaGraph` / `EncoderCudaGraphManager`, with no new config fields, env vars or manager changes.

### Problem

`cudagraph_mm_encoder` graphs the vision towers (Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL, ...), but the Qwen3-Omni audio tower always runs eagerly. ASR clips are short (~100–3,000 encoder tokens), so the audio encoder is launch-bound: 32 layers of small varlen-attention and MLP kernels per call. Under load this shows up as a long encoder tail and higher end-to-end P95/P99.

### Fix

- Split `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder.forward` into three methods, without changing eager behavior:
  - `embed_audio_features`: conv frontend and positional embedding.
  - `prepare_encoder_metadata`: windowed `cu_seqlens` / `max_seqlen`. Eager, capture and replay all use it.
  - `forward_transformer`: layers and output projection, taking only fixed-shape tensors.
- Add `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoderCudaGraphMixin(SupportsEncoderCudaGraph)` to `Qwen3OmniMoeThinkerForConditionalGeneration` and `Qwen3ASRForConditionalGeneration`.
  - Item size is the post-CNN token count. Budgets are auto-generated from one attention window (104 tokens) up to `min(max_num_batched_tokens, max_model_len)`, capped by the existing `encoder_cudagraph_max_token_budget` (default 5,120). Larger batches run eagerly.
  - Capture sizes `cu_seqlens` for the worst-case window count. Padding windows repeat the last offset, the existing cumulative-buffer convention, so padded rows attend to nothing.
  - The graph covers the transformer layers and output MLP. The conv frontend (a few large kernels) stays eager.
- Graphs are enabled only for `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`, whose varlen kernels read `cu_seqlens` on device. `TORCH_SDPA` (host-side split), `FLASHINFER` (needs extra metadata) and `ROCM_AITER_FA` (not yet validated on ROCm) report no graph modalities and stay eager, as today.
- `docs/design/cuda_graphs_multimodal.md`: adds an audio-encoder table.

Not a duplicate:
- #63809 covers the Qwen3-Omni vision tower. This PR covers audio only, and the two dispatch by modality.
- #68083 (FlashInfer audio metadata) is orthogonal; FlashInfer stays eager here.
- #68099 / #68200 (host-side lengths) are already merged, and this PR builds on them.
- #62494 (draft, audio quantization / host sync) and #63379 (LoRA audio projections) also edit `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder.forward`. They address different features; whichever lands second needs a small rebase onto the split methods.

## Results

A Qwen3-Omni (30B-A3B) ASR fine-tune (fp8) with DFlash speculative decoding, 1× B200. Decoder `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, `max_num_seqs=16`. Open-loop Poisson replay of 4,096 real ASR clips (unique `multi_modal_uuids`, no mm cache reuse), 120 s per load step. "Eager FA" is the same backend with `cudagraph_mm_encoder` off, which isolates the graph effect.

| | Eager `TORCH_SDPA` | Eager `FLASH_ATTN` | **This PR** (`FLASH_ATTN` + `cudagraph_mm_encoder`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encoder GPU ms per call, p50 / p95 / p99 | 13.97 / 20.98 / 26.74 | 1.82 / 7.07 / 9.87 | **1.89 / 2.20 / 2.65** |
| E2E P50 / P95 / P99 ms at 58 req/s | 137.0 / 363.5 / 599.8 | 63.1 / 166.5 / 298.9 | **57.1 / 153.3 / 250.2** |
| E2E P50 / P95 / P99 ms at 80 req/s | 219.0 / 560.2 / 877.2 | 73.7 / 198.5 / 430.2 | **63.5 / 171.8 / 334.5** (run 2: 62.2 / 163.7 / 289.6) |
| Requests over the 32-in-flight client cap at 80 req/s | 566 | 61 | **7** (run 2: 3) |
| Exact-match vs reference outputs (temperature 0) | 0.767 | 0.766 | 0.771 (run 2: 0.768) |
| Spec-decode acceptance | 0.503 | 0.502 | 0.509 (run 2: 0.497) |
| Encoder graph capture at startup | – | – | 34 graphs, 1.73 s, 322 MiB |

- The eager SDPA run ran on a slower host CPU, so its absolute latency is pessimistic.
- Graph hits and misses: 32k hits, 0 misses per run.
- Total engine init is 488–552 s in all configs, so encoder capture is under 0.4% of startup.
- `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` with encoder graphs on (`FLASH_ATTN`, 1x B200, commit `43c2b71af4`) raised no GPU↔CPU sync error for Qwen3-ASR-0.6B or Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct: 32 encoder graphs captured, 8 audio clips replayed through graphs, exit 0.

## Public accuracy (eager vs encoder graphs, with an eager-vs-eager control)

Public checkpoints, 1x B200, temperature 0, `FLASH_ATTN` encoder attention, nightly wheel for main `6f022f1080` with this diff applied. Each set was run three times per model: eager, eager again (control), and `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True`. WER is corpus `jiwer` WER after Whisper's `EnglishTextNormalizer`. "Changed" counts utterances whose raw transcript differs from eager run 1.

| Model | Set | N | WER eager / eager (control) / graphs | Changed: control / graphs | Graph hits / misses |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | LibriSpeech test-clean | 2,620 | 2.063 / 2.060 / 2.075% | 17 / 35 | 2620 / 0 |
| Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | LibriSpeech test-other | 2,939 | 4.436 / 4.438 / 4.426% | 39 / 67 | 2939 / 0 |
| Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | ESB VoxPopuli | 1,842 | 6.952 / 6.930 / 6.943% | 27 / 34 | 1827 / 15 |
| Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | ESB AMI | 12,643 | 15.966 / 15.956 / 15.958% | 227 / 328 | 12643 / 0 |
| Qwen3-ASR-0.6B | ESB Earnings-22 | 2,741 | 11.334 / 11.299 / 11.330% | 86 / 146 | 2741 / 0 |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct | LibriSpeech test-clean | 2,620 | 1.414 / 1.412 / 1.429% | 56 / 74 | 2620 / 0 |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct | LibriSpeech test-other | 2,939 | 2.919 / 2.989 / 2.938% | 50 / 123 | 2939 / 0 |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct | ESB VoxPopuli | 1,842 | 6.595 / 6.591 / 6.600% | 57 / 87 | 1842 / 0 |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct | ESB AMI | 12,643 | 11.107 / 11.112 / 11.139% | 187 / 447 | 12643 / 0 |
| Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct | ESB Earnings-22 | 2,741 | 10.054 / 10.048 / 10.081% | 86 / 161 | 2741 / 0 |

- WER with graphs stays within eager run-to-run variation: the largest gap from eager run 1 is 0.03 pp with graphs vs 0.07 pp for the eager control.
- Graphs change more raw transcripts than a second eager run (pooled over 22,785 utterances: Qwen3-ASR 2.68% vs 1.74%, Qwen3-Omni 3.91% vs 1.91%). The likely cause is that graph replay pads each batch to a fixed token budget, so kernels see different shapes and bf16 rounding differs (not isolated further). The changes do not move WER.
- The 15 Qwen3-ASR VoxPopuli misses ran through the eager fallback; all other sets replayed a graph for every utterance.
- ESB sets are from `hf-audio/esb-datasets-test-only-sorted`; TED-LIUM was skipped because its test split fails to load.

## Test plan

Unit tests (real `Qwen3OmniMoeAudioEncoder` with tiny widths, single-rank parallel state) in `tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py`:
- CPU: windowing and metadata padding, item specs vs `_get_feat_extract_output_lengths`, per-item selection, capture `cu_seqlens` covering the worst case.
- GPU: graph replay equals eager for 1-, 3- and 8-clip batches with zero misses. No stale rows after a larger replay through shared buffers. An oversized batch falls back to eager.

E2E test `tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_audio_encoder_cudagraph.py` (`core_model`, selected by the existing "Multimodal Models (Standard)" step): `Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-0.6B` greedy logprobs, eager vs `cudagraph_mm_encoder`, `check_logprobs_close`, on `FLASH_ATTN` and `TRITON_ATTN`.

Results on commit `4f222fe128` (this branch, rebased on main `6f022f1080`). GPU runs: 1× B200, nightly wheel `82c6b325b` with this diff applied. The touched files are unchanged between `82c6b325b` and main.

```
# 1x B200
$ pytest -q -rs tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -k Qwen3OmniAudio
15 passed, 147 deselected, 41 warnings in 29.01s
$ pytest -q -rs -x tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_audio_encoder_cudagraph.py
2 passed, 7 warnings in 229.17s (0:03:49)

# CPU (GPU tests skip)
$ pytest -q tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py
119 passed, 43 skipped in 20.51s

# Eager regression for the split forward: main 6f022f1080 vs this branch, graphs off, 1x B200
$ pytest -q tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py
main:   147 passed in 116.67s (0:01:56)
branch: 162 passed, 40 warnings in 70.03s (0:01:10)
$ pytest -q tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_asr.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_audio_in_video.py tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py
main:   113 passed, 156 warnings in 212.22s (0:03:32)

$ pytest -q tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation.py -k qwen3 --asyncio-mode=auto
main:   2 passed, 12 deselected in 243.68s (0:04:03)

# Greedy outputs + top-5 logprobs, 8 clips (2 vLLM audio assets + 6 LibriSpeech dummy), Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct, FLASH_ATTN

$ pre-commit run --from-ref HEAD~1 --to-ref HEAD

```

## Anticipated review questions

- **Does the manager stay model-agnostic?** Yes. There are no manager, config or runner changes; everything is in the model mixin (#35963, #42785).
- **Is the same metadata used for eager, capture and replay?** Yes, `prepare_encoder_metadata()` (#35963).
- **Do users have to choose budgets?** No. They are auto-generated, and `encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets` still overrides them (#35963).
- **Does the graph cover the bottleneck?** Yes: the 32 layers plus the output MLP are where launch cost dominates. The conv frontend is cheap and stays eager (#43586).
- **Can padding leak into outputs or add quadratic work?** No. Padded windows are empty (repeated offsets), attention is window-local, and a stale-row replay test covers it (#56277, #65453).
- **Oversized batches?** The manager falls back to eager, which is tested (#60112).
- **`encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch` is a vision name.** Agreed. It still caps audio items here; a modality-neutral alias is a manager-wide follow-up (#66662).
- **Why not FlashInfer or SDPA?** SDPA splits on host lengths, and FlashInfer metadata is #68083's scope. Both stay eager until they are graph-safe.
- **Conflict with #63809 (vision graphs)?** Whichever lands second makes `get_input_modality` dispatch on the kwargs keys. It is a small rebase.
- **Size?** +276 / −10 in the model file: 177 lines of protocol mixin (mirrors `encoder_cudagraph_utils.py`) and 89 lines of encoder split.
- **CI cost?** Unit tests run in ~30 s on 1 GPU. The e2e test is one 0.6B model × 2 backends, about 4 min.

## Limitations / follow-ups

- `TORCH_SDPA`, `FLASHINFER` and `ROCM_AITER_FA` stay eager for audio. FlashInfer can be enabled once #68083 lands; `ROCM_AITER_FA` is a one-line addition once it is tested on ROCm.
- The conv frontend stays eager by design.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Honor batch invariance in manual FlashInfer norm fusion
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make the manual FlashInfer all-reduce + RMSNorm helpers honor `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, preventing a batch-size-dependent switch between fused and explicit all-reduce + norm arithmetic. Fixes #68587; extracted from #66088 for independent review.

## Claims

- The shared FlashInfer eligibility predicate rejects fusion in BI mode for both standard RMSNorm and Gemma-style RMSNorm.
- A two-GPU regression test checks exact normalized-output and residual equality against explicit all-reduce + norm, then compares a target row alone and at both ends of a larger batch.
- The test is selected by the optional B200 nightly distributed CI step.

## Validation

### Focused regression on the new base

Base: `9c1d45c21836370104d4eb51d3b46eda20719c47`. The following runs used that commit plus the new tests, first without and then with the production guard. These were working-tree patch runs; the final committed-source check is recorded separately below.

Environment: 2 NVIDIA B200 GPUs, TP=2, BF16 inputs of hidden size 6144; PyTorch `2.16.0.dev20261009+cu134`, CUDA 13.4, FlashInfer **`0.7.2.post1`**. The editable source and native-extension imports were verified outside the checkout. The supplied environment differs from the repository pins; the repository-pinned environment was not tested.

Run the same command from each checkout, replacing only the generic interpreter path:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \
  /path/to/vllm-venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/kernels/core/test_fused_allreduce_gemma_rms_norm.py -k batch_invariant
```

The test itself sets `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` before spawning both ranks; the outer environment above matches the recorded command.

| Source state | Exact pytest summary |
| --- | --- |
| Base + regression tests, guard absent | `2 failed, 18 deselected, 17 warnings in 44.85s` |
| Base + regression tests + guard | `2 passed, 18 deselected, 17 warnings in 52.06s` |

Both unguarded cases (`rms` and `gemma`) fail at the **single-row output versus explicit all-reduce + norm reference** assertion:

```text
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not equal!
Mismatched elements: 1193 / 6144 (19.4%)
Greatest absolute difference: 0.03125 at index (0, 4246)
Greatest relative difference: 0.0078125 at index (0, 268)
```

Those failing cases do not reach the batch-equality assertions. With the guard, both the reference checks and the target-row comparisons at positions 0 and 8191 pass for normalized outputs and returned residuals.

Final committed-source verification: `e9034f75e107607bfe25026346e33e3f6ead02c9`.

The same command on this clean final commit reports:

```text
2 passed, 18 deselected, 17 warnings in 56.77s
```

Existing BI-disabled TP1/TP2 coverage on the same patch before commit:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0 VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 \

commits.pr_title: [Attention][FlashInfer] DiffusionGemma: mixed causal/bidirectional attention on TRTLLM-Gen, default for text-only SM100/SM103
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

DiffusionGemma batches mix causal requests (prompt and commit) with bidirectional requests (denoise). On SM100-family GPUs, vLLM had no fast backend for these batches:
- FlashInfer rejected the model.
- The default backend, FA4, fails at startup because its per-request causal mask is SM90-only.

So B200 users had to pass `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.

This PR runs the mixed batches on FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen and makes that the default for text-only serving (`--language-model-only`) on SM100-family GPUs. It needs https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4905 (VariableWindow FMHA), which is in FlashInfer 0.7.3 and later (vLLM pins 0.7.4).

**Scope:** SM100 family, text-only serving. Hopper and multimodal serving keep their current backend choice.

## Claims

- **Perf:** 1.10–1.45× (BF16 KV) and 1.15–1.54× (FP8 KV) output tokens/s per GPU over `TRITON_ATTN` with BF16 KV, on 1×B200 at concurrency 1–8.
- **Accuracy:** GPQA-Diamond scores 68.69 (BF16 KV) and 69.67 (FP8 KV), against 69.95 for `TRITON_ATTN`.
- **Default:** `vllm serve <diffusiongemma> --language-model-only` now selects FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen on SM100 with no attention flag. Before this PR it failed to start.

## Validation

Model `nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4`, 1×B200, TP1, on `main` at `7dadcb647e` with FlashInfer 0.7.4 and vLLM's default block size.

**Perf.** aiperf with SPEED-Bench 1K-throughput prompts: 32 requests per concurrency level, ISL ≈ 1.2K, OSL ≈ 3.1K, prefix caching off. Each cell is output tokens/s per GPU / per user, the mean of 3 runs. The per-GPU speedup is in parentheses. FP8 KV also runs the query in FP8.

| Concurrency | `TRITON_ATTN`, BF16 KV | TRTLLM-Gen, BF16 KV | TRTLLM-Gen, FP8 KV |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1861 / 2356 | 2055 / 2597 (1.10×) | 2138 / 2615 (1.15×) |
| 2 | 2309 / 1477 | 2902 / 1873 (1.26×) | 3053 / 1905 (1.32×) |
| 4 | 2620 / 859 | 3809 / 1205 (1.45×) | 3931 / 1257 (1.50×) |
| 8 | 2926 / 504 | 3911 / 689 (1.34×) | 4493 / 740 (1.54×) |

**Accuracy.** GPQA-Diamond with NeMo-Skills: AA `mcq-4choices` prompt, thinking on, pass@1 averaged over 16 runs. The model card reports 68.6 for NVFP4. The `TRITON_ATTN` row is from an earlier base.

| Attention | KV cache | pass@1 |
|---|---|---|
| `TRITON_ATTN` | BF16 | 69.95 |
| FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen | BF16 | 68.69 |
| FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen | FP8 | 69.67 |

No-answer rates are 3.6–4.7% across the three configs.

**Long-input TTFT.** At `84ec2da850`, concurrency 1, prefix caching off, one 256-token canvas; median TTFT in seconds over 10 requests, speedup over `TRITON_ATTN` with the same KV dtype in parentheses.

| ISL | `TRITON_ATTN`, BF16 KV | TRTLLM-Gen, BF16 KV | `TRITON_ATTN`, FP8 KV | TRTLLM-Gen, FP8 KV |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16K | 1.14 | 0.71 (1.61×) | 1.30 | 0.56 (2.33×) |
| 32K | 2.35 | 1.20 (1.96×) | 2.66 | 0.81 (3.29×) |
| 64K | 5.94 | 2.55 (2.33×) | 6.95 | 1.51 (4.60×) |

**Other checks:**
- **Tests:** `tests/kernels/attention/test_mixed_causal_attn.py` gives 16 passed, 4 skipped (FA4 cases are Hopper-only); `test_attention_selector.py` gives 88 passed, 14 skipped.
- **Default selection, no attention flag:** with `--language-model-only`, both BF16 and FP8 KV select FlashInfer TRTLLM-Gen and answer a smoke prompt correctly. Without it, the selection is unchanged. Explicit `FLASHINFER` with BF16 KV also answers it; with TRTLLM attention off or an NVFP4 KV cache, startup fails.

## Details

- **Sliding-window layers:** per-token KV bounds go to TRTLLM-Gen's VariableWindow kernel. A causal token attends to `[pos - w, pos]` and a bidirectional token to `[pos - w, pos + w]`, matching the FlashAttention reference path.
- **Full-attention layers (head dim 512):** FlashInfer has no VariableWindow kernel for this head dim. The layer runs one causal and one dense launch and keeps each token's own row.
- **Head-dim-512 KV pages:** FlashInfer 0.7.4 has TRTLLM-Gen dynamic-page kernels (128 or more tokens per page) only for head dims 64, 128 and 256. For other head dims the backend offers kernel pages of at most 64 tokens, and vLLM splits larger KV blocks into them. Without this, startup fails with "Missing TRTLLM-GEN kernel".
- **Causal flags:** per-request flags may be bool or int32. DiffusionGemma's persistent buffer is int32.
- **FULL CUDA graphs:** window bounds and causal flags live in persistent builder buffers. Tokens map to requests with `searchsorted`, and padding tokens get `[0, 0]` bounds. The backend keeps reporting `UNIFORM_BATCH`, so the canvas-length denoise steps are captured as FULL graphs.
- **Default backend:** DiffusionGemma's config hook selects `FLASHINFER` with `use_trtllm_attention=True` when all of these hold:
  - no attention backend is set, and TRTLLM attention isn't turned off;
  - serving is text-only (`--language-model-only`, or a checkpoint without a vision tower);
  - the GPU is SM100 family with TRTLLM-Gen available.
- **Explicit `FLASHINFER`:** TRTLLM-Gen attention is forced on. Startup fails with a clear error if it is turned off or unavailable, or with an NVFP4 KV cache.
- **Not supported yet:** quantized attention output on the merged full-attention path, and DCP. Both raise `NotImplementedError`.

<summary>Serve command (perf server)</summary>

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 \
vllm serve nvidia/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it-NVFP4 \
  --language-model-only --enable-expert-parallel --moe-backend auto \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --diffusion-config '{"canvas_length":256}' \

  --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true}' \
  --reasoning-parser gemma4 --tool-call-parser gemma4 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --trust-remote-code
```

- **FP8 KV:** `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
- **Baseline:** `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.
- **GPQA server:** the same, except `--max-num-seqs 4 --max-model-len 65536 --enable-prefix-caching`.
- `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` only exposes `/reset_prefix_cache`, which the sweep calls between concurrency levels.

The perf runs passed `--attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER","use_trtllm_attention":true}'`. That is the setting the new default selects.
</details>

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Support HY4 Flash
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable HiSparse for HY4 Flash (`tencent/Hy4-flash`, `HYV4FlashForConditionalGeneration`).

- **HiSparse fix (shared):** HY4 Flash implements its sliding-window layers with the sparse MLA kernel over fixed window indices. Their KV belongs to the sliding-window manager, which HiSparse never binds (`get_hisparse_source_layers` only takes full-attention layers). They still received HiSparse cache handles, and the first KV write failed. Sliding-window sparse layers now register a plain index group, so only real HiSparse sources get handles. This applies to any model that mixes sliding-window and DSA layers.
- **Model guard:** HY4 Flash rejected any KV transfer config. It now accepts `HiSparseConnector`; other connectors and LoRA are still rejected.

DFly with HiSparse stays rejected by DFly's own KV-connector guard. Supporting it needs the draft layers to share the target layers' HiSparse state, which is left for a follow-up.

## Repro on `main` (`e2bab26e51`)

```bash
vllm serve tencent/Hy4-flash-FP8 -tp 8 --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32768 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 1G \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}}'
```

- **As is:** `ValueError: HYV4 Flash does not support KV transfer or LoRA` (`hy_v4_flash/nvidia/model.py:47`).
- **With only that guard removed:** warmup fails with `AssertionError` in `HiSparseCacheHandle.write_target` (`vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py:1194`), reached from a sliding-window layer's KV write.

## Test plan

8×H200, TP8, `tencent/Hy4-flash-FP8`, bf16 KV, CUDA graphs on. The command is the repro above; the baseline drops the last two flags.

- GSM8K: `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --use-chat-completions --num-questions 300 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 32 --temperature 0 --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"no_think"}'`

- Unit test: `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse_skips_sliding_window` fails on `main` (the layer gets a `HiSparseCacheHandle`) and passes with this PR.

## Test results

| | Baseline (no HiSparse) | HiSparse (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 0.897 | 0.910 |
| Long-context retrieval | – | 16/16 |
| Needle at 9k / 17k / 29k tokens | pass | pass |

commits.pr_title: [Feature] Encoder-only attention hooks for model-owned layouts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Three small hooks that let a model (an in-tree model file or a plugin) own its encoder attention without changes to shared code, following the model-owned pattern of #63114 (`get_model_state_cls()`). They come out of the review of #65268: the segment attention layout there can live in a model-owned state, backend and pooler once these hooks exist.

| hook | change |
|---|---|
| `EncoderOnlyAttention(attn_backend=...)` | a given backend replaces the selected one and is wrapped for non-causal metadata like a selected one. It skips the selector and its validation and overrides `--attention-backend`; a warning names the backend used and the `--attention-backend` it overrides, and checking the given backend fits the head size, dtype, KV cache dtype and platform is the caller's job. Its `get_name()` must be a registered `AttentionBackendEnum` name. Threaded through `BertModel` / `BertPoolingModel` / `BertEncoder` / `BertLayer` / `BertAttention` / `BertSelfAttention`; only the BERT classes take `attn_backend=` |
| `FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder._make_metadata(**kwargs)` | creates the metadata `build` returns and builds the block mask of, so a subclass can return its own metadata (e.g. another `get_mask_mod`) filled from per-builder data, without the stock mask being built first |
| `register_model_config()` | next to `MODELS_CONFIG_MAP`, exported next to `ModelRegistry`, so a plugin can register its config hook; like `ModelRegistry.register_model`, a later registration overwrites, with a warning if it replaces a different hook |

Wrapped attention backends (`subclass_attention_backend*`) now keep the underlying class's `__module__` and a prefixed `__qualname__`. Attention groups are keyed by `full_cls_name()`, so a model's own backend with the same class name as a stock one (e.g. a plugin's `FlexAttentionBackend`) gets its own group instead of silently sharing the stock one.

No behaviour change when the hooks are not used: the defaults are the current backend selection, `FlexAttentionMetadata` and the existing map.

A model-owned Flex backend next to stock FlexAttention layers (two Flex groups) needs #63985; without it the engine fails at startup. The end-to-end test's case with stock FlexAttention layers is skipped with that reason until #63985 lands.

## Tests

`tests/v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks.py` (CPU):

- `EncoderOnlyAttention` uses a given backend (no re-selection), wraps it as encoder-only, and logs a warning naming it and the `--attention-backend` it overrides;
- a backend with the same class name from another module gets a distinct `full_cls_name()` when wrapped;
- every encoder layer of `BertModel` and `BertPoolingModel` receives the backend;
- a `FlexAttentionMetadataBuilder` subclass's `_make_metadata` returns its metadata and the block mask is built from its mask; two builders of one class keep their own per-builder data;
- `register_model_config` registers, is idempotent, and overwrites a different hook with a warning.

`tests/v1/attention/test_encoder_only_attention_hooks_e2e.py` (GPU, through `LLM`): a BERT model registered in-process (MiniLM weights) runs its own Flex backend and metadata (causal within each request) on layers 0-2 and the selected backend on layers 3-5, eager and default mode. Its token embeddings must match a Transformers reference that applies the two masks per layer, and the stock model must match the one-mask reference.

Results on beff776cae (1x GB300, nightly wheel of the base commit 2497008666 + the PR's files):

| check | result |
|---|---|
| both test files in one process | 10 passed, 2 skipped (stock-Flex case, needs #63985) |
| e2e max diff (FP32, normalized) | stock vs reference 3.2e-4; mixed vs two-mask reference 3.3e-4; mixed vs one-mask reference 2.1e-1 |
| e2e incl. stock-Flex case with #63985 applied | 4 passed |
| stock-Flex case without #63985 | fails at startup (CUDA graph output overwritten), as expected |
| stock models, PR vs base, TRITON_ATTN (`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`) | bitwise equal: MiniLM, bge-base; eager and default |
| stock models, PR vs base, FLEX_ATTENTION | bge-base bitwise equal (eager, default); MiniLM within run-to-run noise (base vs base up to 1.1e-4, PR runs inside that range) |
| full `pre-commit` on the changed files (incl. mypy) | clean |

Related: #65268, #63114, #63985.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Apply the e4m3fnuz KV-scale factor for compressed-tensors

## Overview

On gfx94x GPUs (MI300 series), FP8 is `e4m3fnuz`, whose largest value is 240 instead of `e4m3fn`'s 448, so a scale calibrated for `e4m3fn` has to be doubled. `BaseKVCacheMethod` does this. `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod.process_weights_after_loading` replaces that hook without calling `super()`, so compressed-tensors checkpoints with calibrated FP8 KV-cache scales run with half the scale there and clip keys at the FP8 cache write. This PR applies the ×2 when building `_k_scale` / `_v_scale` / `_q_scale`, for a configured `kv_cache_scheme`, and to `q_scale` only when the checkpoint provides one.

## Claims

- On fnuz platforms, with a `kv_cache_scheme` and a quantized KV cache, the `_k/_v/_q_scale` buffers and the float and host copies derived from them are twice the loaded scales, as `BaseKVCacheMethod` makes them. A checkpoint without `q_scale` keeps 1.0.
- On MI300X (gfx942), the share of keys that saturate in the fp8 KV cache drops from 0.9–1.5% to under 0.001%, and GSM8K-text perplexity with the fp8 KV cache is within 0.7% of a bf16 KV cache, against up to 20.5% on main (table below).
- No change off fnuz platforms, without a `kv_cache_scheme` (the scales keep their 1.0 default), or for an unquantized KV cache. Running the hook again does not compound the factor.

## Validation

Unit test `test_compressed_tensors_kv_scales_fnuz_doubling` in `tests/quantization/test_compressed_tensors.py`, with no ROCm skip, so the H200 Quantization job runs it. It monkeypatches `is_fp8_fnuz`. Four cases: fnuz with `q_scale`, fnuz without `q_scale`, not fnuz, and fnuz without a scheme.

```

| no, none or set | pass | pass |
| yes, none | pass | pass |
| yes, set (with and without `q_scale`) | fail: `assert 0.30000001192092896 == 0.6 ± 6.0e-07` | pass |

End-to-end on MI300X (gfx942), same image, with `repro.py` below: perplexity over 32 windows of 1,024 tokens of GSM8K train text, prefilled in 128-token chunks. The reference is the same checkpoint with `kv_cache_dtype=bfloat16` on `TRITON_ATTN`: 3.8982 for TinyLlama, 3.6956 for Llama-3.2-1B.

Using gfx950 (MI350, stock behavior) as the ground truth, we compare gfx942 results before and after the fix.

```python
"""Layer-0 KV scales, saturated keys and GSM8K-text perplexity for vllm#66586."""

import math
import os
import sys

os.environ["VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING"] = "0"

from datasets import load_dataset  # noqa: E402

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams  # noqa: E402
from vllm.inputs import TokensPrompt  # noqa: E402
from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import Attention  # noqa: E402

FP8_MAX = 240.0  # e4m3fnuz

model, backend, kv_cache_dtype = sys.argv[1:4]
llm = LLM(
    model,
    kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
    attention_config={"backend": backend},
    enforce_eager=True,
    max_model_len=2048,
    max_num_batched_tokens=128,
    max_num_seqs=64,
    enable_prefix_caching=False,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.2,
    seed=0,
)
saturated = [0, 0]


def setup(model):
    layers = [m for m in model.modules() if isinstance(m, Attention)]

    def count(layer, args):
        ratio = args[1].float().abs() / layer._k_scale.float()
        saturated[0] += int((ratio > FP8_MAX).sum())
        saturated[1] += ratio.numel()

    for layer in layers:
        layer.register_forward_pre_hook(count)
    a = layers[0]
    return a.kv_cache_dtype, a.k_scale.item(), a._k_scale_float, a._q_scale_float


kv, k_ckpt, k_used, q_used = llm.apply_model(setup)[0]
print(f"layer 0: kv_cache={kv} k_scale={k_ckpt:.6g} _k_scale_float={k_used:.6g} "
      f"_q_scale_float={q_used:.6g}")

tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
rows = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="train")
windows, ids, i = [], [], 0
while len(windows) < 32:
    text = f"Question: {rows[i]['question']}\nAnswer: {rows[i]['answer']}\n\n"
    ids += tok(text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    i += 1
    if len(ids) >= 1024:
        windows.append([tok.bos_token_id] + ids[:1024])
        ids = []

params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=1, temperature=0.0, prompt_logprobs=0)
outs = llm.generate([TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=w) for w in windows], params)
nll = [-o.prompt_logprobs[j][w[j]].logprob for w, o in zip(windows, outs)
       for j in range(1, len(w))]
sat = f"{100 * saturated[0] / saturated[1]:.3f}%" if kv.startswith("fp8") else "n/a"
ppl = math.exp(sum(nll) / len(nll))
print(f"saturated keys: {sat}  GSM8K-text perplexity: {ppl:.4f}")
```

saturated keys: n/a  GSM8K-text perplexity: 3.6956
```

</details>

## Details

- `BaseKVCacheMethod` initialises scales to a `-1.0` sentinel and doubles only loaded ones. Here k/v default to 1.0, so a configured `kv_cache_scheme`, the same test `create_weights` uses, stands in for "loaded"; `validate_kv_cache_scheme` limits it to 8-bit float. A checkpoint that declares a scheme but ships no k/v scales would get 2.0 instead of 1.0; llm-compressor writes the two together. KV-only checkpoints ship no `q_scale`, so `q_scale` starts at the `-1.0` sentinel and is doubled only when loaded.
- The factor goes into the buffer copies rather than the `k_scale` parameters, because a weight reload runs this hook again. `_k_scale` is now a scaled copy, not an alias of `k_scale`.
- Multiplying by the factor allocates a new tensor, so registering it would move `_k/_v/_q_scale` away from the addresses captured CUDA graphs read. Once registered, they are written with `copy_`, as the previous `detach()` view kept them in place. Only the first load registers, because the default shape is `()`.
- `test_compressed_tensors_kv_scales_fnuz_doubling` has no ROCm skip. The H200 Quantization job runs `quantization/`, so it runs these four cases. The MI300 and MI355 Quantization steps also run that directory and stay optional.
- Not a duplicate: no open, merged or closed PR applies the fnuz factor to compressed-tensors KV scales (checked open PRs touching `compressed_tensors.py` and `quantization/kv_cache.py`, and PR and issue text for `CompressedTensorsKVCacheMethod` and `fnuz`). #66519 (open) adds an early return for unquantized KV caches at the top of this method, and three Fast Start drafts (#63673, #63976, #64738) edit it too; none adds the factor, and they will conflict textually.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MoE] Add AITER Triton MXFP8 MoE backend for gfx942
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds the `aiter_triton_mxfp8_mxfp8` MoE backend, so MXFP8 MoE models run on MI300X / MI325X (gfx942) with their expert weights kept in MXFP8. Today these models fall back to `EMULATION` on gfx942, which unpacks every expert weight to BF16.

vLLM picks it automatically on gfx942. `--moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp8_mxfp8` pins it. Needs ROCm/aiter#6219, which ships in the current nightly (aiter `0.1.29`).

## Results

On `tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8`, TP8, MI325X, compared with the current nightly:

- Expert weights take about half the memory: 109 GiB per GPU instead of 196 GiB. This is what lets Hy4 fit on 192 GB MI300X.
- 4x more KV cache (2.69M tokens instead of 688K).
- 13 to 23% more output throughput at 8K, 32K and 128K input.
- Same GSM8K accuracy (96.8% on both).

### Hy4-preview-FP8, TP8

| | Nightly (`EMULATION`) | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Model memory per GPU | 195.8 GiB | **109.1 GiB** |
| KV cache | 688K tokens | **2.69M tokens** |
| GSM8K, 5-shot, 1319 questions | 96.82% | 96.82% |

| Input / output / concurrency | Output tok/s | TTFT | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8K / 1K / 16 | 308.9 → **369.0** (+19%) | 5.3 → 5.4 s | 46.7 → **38.1 ms** |
| 32K / 1K / 16 | 174.4 → **197.7** (+13%) | 14.3 → 14.5 s | 77.7 → **66.7 ms** |
| 128K / 1K / 8 | 46.1 → **56.5** (+23%) | 82.6 → **42.0 s** | **84.5** → 100.4 ms |

At 128K the time per token goes up while total throughput still goes up. My guess is that faster prefill lets more requests decode at the same time, but I have not confirmed it.

### MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4

This checkpoint ships NVFP4 experts, which ROCm can't run directly, so vLLM requantizes them at load with `--quantization-config.moe`.

| MoE setting | GSM8K | 8K / 1K / 16 | 32K / 1K / 16 | 128K / 1K / 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mxfp8`, nightly (`EMULATION`) | did not finish (1 h 27 min for 88%) | 24.5 tok/s | 23.0 tok/s* | 10.7 tok/s* |
| `mxfp8`, this PR | 95.91% | 453.8 tok/s | 266.1 tok/s | 85.6 tok/s |
| `fp8_per_channel`, nightly (AITER FP8) | 95.83% | 536.2 tok/s | 308.3 tok/s | 100.1 tok/s |

\* single batch only; the full run was too slow.

With `mxfp8` this PR is 8 to 18x faster than today. `fp8_per_channel` is still about 15% faster on MiniMax, so it stays the better choice there. The real target is checkpoints like Hy4 that ship MXFP8 weights.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

All runs on MI325X with real weights and prefix caching off. Baselines use the same commands on the current nightly without `--moe-backend` (the MiniMax `fp8_per_channel` row uses `--quantization-config.moe fp8_per_channel`).

**Hy4-preview-FP8 (TP8)**

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve tencent/Hy4-preview-FP8 \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --reasoning-parser hy_v4 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp8_mxfp8
```

**MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (TP4)**

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1

vllm serve MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --language-model-only \
    --max-model-len 136000 \
    --max-num-seqs 32 \
    --block-size 128 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
    --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"fp8"}' \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager \
    --quantization-config.moe mxfp8 \
    --moe-backend aiter_triton_mxfp8_mxfp8
```

**Throughput** (concurrency 16 at 8K and 32K input, 8 at 128K)

```bash
vllm bench serve \
    --backend vllm \
    --model <model> \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len <input_len> \
    --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0 \
    --max-concurrency <concurrency> \
    --num-prompts <4 x concurrency> \
    --ignore-eos \
    --seed 0
```

**GSM8K**

```bash
lm_eval \
    --model local-chat-completions \
    --model_args model=<model>,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=64 \
    --tasks gsm8k \
    --num_fewshot 5 \
    --apply_chat_template \
    --fewshot_as_multiturn \
    --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=16384,temperature=0
```

For Hy4, the GSM8K task's `Question:` stop string is removed. Hy4 often writes `Question:` in its reasoning, which cuts the answer short and scores it as empty (see #57526).

</details>

## How it works

MXFP8 is FP8 numbers with one shared scale per 32 values. MI350 applies those scales inside the matrix multiply. MI300 can't, which is why vLLM unpacks everything to BF16 there today.

MI300 does have fast FP8 matrix multiply, though. The AITER kernel from ROCm/aiter#6219 multiplies each 32-value chunk in plain FP8 and applies that chunk's scale to the result. Same math, weights stay at 1 byte each, nothing is unpacked.

MI300 also reads FP8 slightly differently (`e4m3fnuz` instead of the checkpoint's `e4m3fn`): the same bits are worth exactly half. So at load we add 1 to each shared scale exponent and leave the weight bytes alone. No extra copy, no precision loss.

## What changed

- `fused_moe/experts/aiter_mxfp8_moe.py`: the new `AiterTritonMxfp8ExpertsMonolithic`, next to the existing gfx950 AITER MXFP8 experts. AITER routes and sorts the tokens, then runs two `moe_gemm_a8w8` calls with vLLM's activation in between. Works with CUDA graphs and routed-experts capture.
- `oracle/fp8.py`, `oracle/mxfp8.py`, `config/kernel.py`: register the backend. On gfx942 it is picked ahead of `EMULATION`. `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` turns it off.
- `quantization/utils/mxfp8_utils.py`: the load-time `e4m3fn` to `e4m3fnuz` conversion.
- `quantization/online/mxfp8.py`: `--quantization-config.moe '{"weight":"mxfp8","activation":"mxfp8"}'` now works. Other activation choices get a clear error.
- `inc_mxfp8_moe.py`: adds `apply_monolithic`, since INC MXFP8 can now get this backend on gfx942.
- Docs and the Hy4-preview recipe: mention the backend for MI325X.

## Tests

Run locally on MI325X. The kernel tests live in `tests/kernels/moe`, which the existing MI300 MoE shards already run.

- `test_ocp_mx_moe.py`: `test_rocm_mxfp8_moe_oracle`, the MXFP8 counterpart of `test_rocm_mxfp4_moe_oracle`, checks the backend against `torch_experts` across routing methods, activations, router weight on input and token counts. Also checks the `e4m3fn` to `e4m3fnuz` conversion bit for bit.
- `test_mxfp8_aiter_backend_selection.py`: when the backend is picked and when it isn't.
- `test_online.py`, `test_auto_round.py`: online MXFP8 dispatch and INC.

## Limitations

- gfx942 only. MI350 already has its own AITER MXFP8 path.
- TP only, no EP or EPLB yet.
- No expert bias or fused shared experts. Those fall back to `EMULATION`.
