commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] benchmark_moe: keep HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES for Ray
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #65919. On ROCm, `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py` renames `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` before `ray.init()`. Since Ray 2.45 (ray-project/ray#51104), Ray selects AMD GPUs with `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and raises `RuntimeError: Please use HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES instead of ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` when only `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is set. So with any Ray version vLLM tests against (`requirements/test/rocm.in` pins `>=2.56.0,<2.57`), setting `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` makes the benchmark and `--tune` fail.

## Changes

- Remove the rename; `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is passed to Ray as set.
- In `BenchmarkWorker.tune`, read `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` instead of `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES` for the device-guard check, since that is what Ray sets in each worker now. Either way, the worker runs on its local device 0.
- With several GPUs (`HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1`), drop the `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` copy that importing vLLM makes, before `ray.init()`. Otherwise workers inherit it, and their own vLLM import raises because it doesn't match the narrower `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` Ray gives them. Suggested and tested by @giuseppegrossi.

## Validation

### On AMD hardware (run by @giuseppegrossi)

2x Radeon RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce39` (vLLM 0.32.1rc1, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0), Ray 2.59.0 and 2.56.1. `benchmark_moe.py --model Qwen/Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B --tp-size 1`, with the PCI bus printed inside each Ray worker and checked against `rocm-smi`.

On `main`, setting `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to `0`, `1` or `0,1` fails at `ray.init()` on both Ray versions, in benchmark and `--tune` mode, with `RuntimeError: Please use HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES instead of ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`. Leaving it unset works.

With this PR:

| `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` | Mode | Ray | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | benchmark | 2.59.0 | Pass; runs only on card 0 |
| `1` | benchmark | 2.59.0 | Pass; runs only on card 1, card 0 stays idle |
| `0,1` | benchmark | 2.59.0 | Pass; one worker per card |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Prefetch the whole checkpoint into every node's page cache
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Safetensors prefetch (`--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch`, or the automatic prefetch on NFS/Lustre) splits the checkpoint shards by **global** rank. The page cache is per node, so on a multi-node deployment each node warms only `1/num_nodes` of the shards, and its ranks then read the rest cold through the loader. This PR splits the shards among the ranks of **each node**, so every node prefetches the whole checkpoint.

This affects any deployment whose world group spans nodes with prefetch active:
- TP or PP across nodes (`--nnodes`, or Ray);
- DP/EP across nodes, because `init_distributed_environment` folds the DP rank into the global rank.

Related: #51339 (extends auto-prefetch to VirtioFS), #49324 (prefetch in the multi-thread loader; it calls `_prefetch_all_checkpoints`, so it inherits this fix), #57973, and the earlier prefetch and read-order work in #40068, #41499, #42837.

Follow-ups: #68490 (stacked on this PR: EP-aware prefetch plus a per-node RAM gate) and #68491 (enable the EP weight filter by default).

## Claims

- Each node now prefetches every shard. With 4 ranks per node, a rank prefetches 23–24 of 94 shards, instead of 11–12 (2 nodes) or 5–6 (4 nodes).
- Model loading on the slowest node, **stock → this PR** (median of all cold starts), Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8:
  - TP8, 2 nodes: **244.7 s → 78.3 s (−68%)**
  - DEP16, 4 nodes: **105.5 s → 43.2 s (−59%)**
  - TEP8, 2 nodes: **63.9 s → 47.5 s (−26%)**
- Time to `/health` ready: TP8 **395.5 s → 225.3 s (−43%)**, DEP16 **280.4 s → 220.3 s (−21%)**, TEP8 217.9 s → 203.8 s (−6%).
- Outputs are unchanged: greedy completions are bit-identical between arms under TP8 and TEP8. Single-node behaviour is unchanged.

## Validation

### Unit test

`tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_prefetch_checkpoints.py` simulates `(nodes, ranks per node)` in `{(1,1), (1,4), (2,4), (4,2)}` and asserts that the files prefetched by each node's ranks together cover the whole checkpoint. I ran it in the same image as the A/B, with the stock `weight_utils.py` and then with this PR's version bind-mounted over it:

```
== stock
FAILED test_prefetch_checkpoints.py::test_each_node_prefetches_all_files[2-4]
FAILED test_prefetch_checkpoints.py::test_each_node_prefetches_all_files[4-2]
2 failed, 2 passed in 6.29s
== patched
4 passed in 6.45s
```

### End-to-end A/B

**Setup**
- Hardware: nodes of 4 GPUs (GB300-class, aarch64, ~800 GiB free RAM each) on a Lustre shared filesystem.
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai:cu134-nightly-f5d93296c8ec82b7e7dabdb308d24d43cb1907bf`. Its `weight_utils.py` is identical to f5d93296c8.
- **Arms:** A is the stock image. Fix is the same image with this PR's `weight_utils.py` bind-mounted over it.
- **Flags:** `--safetensors-load-strategy prefetch --no-numa-bind --max-model-len 8192`.
- **Cold cache:** before every start, on every node, `posix_fadvise(POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)` was called on all shards, and `mincore` reported **0.00 % resident** afterwards.
- **Starts:** interleaved within each allocation, with a warm torch.compile cache. Each allocation's first, compile-priming start is left out. Metrics are the slowest node's "Model loading took" and the time to `/health` ready.

All runs load **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** (406 GB, 94 shards). Values are the median over cold starts, **stock → this PR**:

| Topology | EP weight filter | Model loading (s) | Time to ready (s) | Starts (stock / PR) | Greedy outputs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8, 2 nodes | n/a | **244.7 → 78.3 (−68%)** | 395.5 → 225.3 (−43%) | 5 / 5 | identical |
| DEP16, 4 nodes | off | **105.5 → 43.2 (−59%)** | 280.4 → 220.3 (−21%) | 3 / 4 | varies run to run in both arms* |
| TEP8, 2 nodes | off | **63.9 → 47.5 (−26%)** | 217.9 → 203.8 (−6%) | 2 / 4 | identical |

| Topology | EP weight filter | Stock | This PR |

| TP8, 2 nodes | n/a | 253.1 / 395.8, 244.7 / 390.9, 246.2 / 390.5, 240.0 / 405.6, 240.7 / 395.5 | 81.0 / 230.4, 78.3 / 220.3, 67.3 / 210.3, 78.8 / 230.4, 67.9 / 225.3 |

The fix's prefetch takes ~16.5 s for 23–24 shards per rank (~24 GB/s per node), against ~8.5 s for 12 shards in arm A. It runs in the background, so the extra prefetch time is repaid many times over by the loader not reading the missing shards cold.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction recipe</summary>

Per start, on every node (outside vLLM):

```python
# evict + verify: posix_fadvise(DONTNEED) on every *.safetensors, then mincore residency
import ctypes, glob, os
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
libc.mmap.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
libc.mmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_long]
libc.munmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t]
libc.mincore.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_ubyte)]
PAGE = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE")
res = tot = 0
for p in sorted(glob.glob(f"{MODEL_DIR}/*.safetensors")):
    fd = os.open(p, os.O_RDONLY)
    os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
    size = os.path.getsize(p); n = (size + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
    addr = libc.mmap(None, size, 1, 1, fd, 0)  # PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED
    vec = (ctypes.c_ubyte * n)(); libc.mincore(addr, size, vec); libc.munmap(addr, size)
    os.close(fd)
    res += sum(v & 1 for v in bytes(vec)); tot += n
print(f"resident={100 * res / tot:.2f}%")
```

Launch, one process per node:

```bash
# TP8 / TEP8 across 2 nodes (TEP8 adds --enable-expert-parallel)
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch --max-model-len 8192 --no-numa-bind \
  --nnodes 2 --node-rank $NODE_RANK --master-addr $HEAD --master-port 29555 \
  $( [ "$NODE_RANK" -gt 0 ] && echo --headless )

# DEP16 across 4 nodes
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --data-parallel-size 16 --data-parallel-size-local 4 --data-parallel-address $HEAD \
  --data-parallel-rpc-port 13345 --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch --max-model-len 8192 --no-numa-bind \
  $( [ "$NODE_RANK" -gt 0 ] && echo --headless --data-parallel-start-rank $((NODE_RANK * 4)) )
```

Poll `http://$HEAD:8000/health` from process start ("ready"). Then send 5 completions (`temperature=0, max_tokens=64`) and hash the JSON. The metrics come from each worker's `Prefetching checkpoint files`, `Loading weights took` and `Model loading took` log lines.

`--no-numa-bind` was used in all arms: in this image, auto NUMA binding asserted during concurrent worker start (`numa_utils._mp_set_executable`), which is unrelated to this PR.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Raw log excerpts, TP8 (A, then fix)</summary>

```
== A, node 1
(Worker_TP4) INFO [weight_utils.py:1087] Prefetching checkpoint files: 100% (12/12)
(Worker_TP4) INFO [weight_utils.py:1110] Prefetching checkpoint files into page cache finished in 8.08s
(Worker_TP4) INFO [default_loader.py:543] Loading weights took 241.70 seconds
(Worker_TP4) INFO [model_runner.py:447] Model loading took 46.78 GiB memory and 245.024109 seconds
(Worker_TP6) INFO [weight_utils.py:1087] Prefetching checkpoint files: 100% (11/11)
== fix, node 1
(Worker_TP4) INFO [weight_utils.py:1090] Prefetching checkpoint files: 100% (24/24)
(Worker_TP4) INFO [weight_utils.py:1113] Prefetching checkpoint files into page cache finished in 16.39s
(Worker_TP4) INFO [default_loader.py:543] Loading weights took 58.65 seconds
(Worker_TP4) INFO [model_runner.py:447] Model loading took 46.78 GiB memory and 61.913839 seconds
(Worker_TP6) INFO [weight_utils.py:1090] Prefetching checkpoint files: 100% (23/23)
```

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `_prefetch_all_checkpoints` took `sorted_files[rank::world_size]` using the global rank. With 2 nodes x 4 ranks, node 0's ranks warmed shards `{i : i % 8 in 0..3}` and node 1's warmed `{i % 8 in 4..7}`. Each rank then reads tensors from every shard, so every node loaded half of its bytes cold. The prefetch was introduced and validated on a single node, where global and local rank coincide.

**Fix.** Use `get_world_group().local_rank` together with `world_size // get_node_count()` as the local rank and local world size, so the ranks of every node together cover all shards. SGLang and TensorRT-LLM split their prefetch the same way, by node-local rank. `% local_world_size` and `max(..., 1)` keep the split well-defined if the world group's ranks are not evenly spread across nodes. The single-process path is unchanged.

**Trade-off.** Each node now reads every shard during the prefetch, whereas each node's loader used to read the missing shards cold. Every node's ranks read from every shard either way, so total filesystem traffic barely changes; it moves from slow, serialized cold loader reads to a parallel background prefetch. For a checkpoint larger than node RAM, the stacked follow-up #68490 prefetches only the node's share under EP.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm] Warm the AITER FA extend kernels from the attention backend
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Register the two `ROCM_AITER_FA` extend kernels from the attention backend's metadata builder, through `JitWarmupRegistry`, so they build at startup instead of on the first chunked-prefill continuation or prefix-cache hit.

## Motivation

A fresh prompt runs one causal varlen call without the LSE. A chunked continuation or prefix-cache hit runs `extend_forward`, which makes a causal call for the new tokens and a noncausal call per gathered context chunk, both returning the LSE. AITER builds each of those modules on first use, so the first request that takes the extend path stalls for about 45 s per module.

The study of which kernels each ROCm attention backend misses, and where a warmup can be registered, is in [#68022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68022).

## Changes

- Register `AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel` from the `ROCM_AITER_FA` metadata builder, with two keys: causal with sinks, and noncausal without sinks. It uses the same `VllmJitKernel` / `JitWarmupRegistry` mechanism as FA4.
- Sliding-window layers register nothing. Their extend path runs the same LSE-free call as a fresh prompt.
- The warmup passes `min_seqlen_q=0`, the same literal the serving calls pass. AITER names the module after a zero value.
- The warmup query is 16 tokens, because AITER treats a one-token query as decode and drops `causal`.
- The registry deduplicates identical layers. Only models that use this backend register the kernels.
- This does not affect Model Runner V1, which this tree no longer ships. The registration runs inside the V2 runner's `initialize_kv_cache`, and `kernel_warmup` compiles it.

## Trade-offs

- On a cold cache, startup pays the AITER build time for the registered modules (about 100 s here for both). A warm AITER build cache makes this cheap. The cost moves from the first extend request to startup.
- This covers the `ROCM_AITER_FA` extend kernels only. Other backends' misses are covered in #68022.
- [#67083](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67083) takes a generic route, calling a cached-context prefill during `warmup_kernels`. The two overlap on these kernels, and maintainers may prefer one.

## Validation

Tiny dummy Llama (2 layers, GQA 8/2), one gfx950 GPU, `ROCM_AITER_FA`, `max_num_batched_tokens=32`, prefix caching on, cold AITER cache. Requests: an 8-token fresh prompt, then a 160-token prompt that gets split (chunked), then the same 160 tokens again (prefix hit).

| Run | Modules built by the chunked request | Chunked request time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Baseline, head dim 64 | `mask_lse`, `nmask_lse` (47 s each) | 93.6 s |
| Baseline, head dim 256 | `mask_lse`, `nmask_lse` (47 s each) | 93.5 s |
| This change, head dim 256 | none; both built during `JIT kernel warmup` (101 s) | 0.06 s |
| This change, head dim 128 | none; uses `module_fmha_v3_varlen_fwd`, which the fresh prompt already builds | 0.05 s |

Unit tests: `tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_fa_extend_warmup.py` (3 tests, 4 cases). One checks that a sliding-window layer registers no keys. One checks the arguments the warmup passes to `flash_attn_varlen_func`, including the causal and context-chunk split and the sink pointer. One builds `AiterFlashAttentionMetadataBuilder` inside an active `JitWarmupRegistry` and checks that `registry.warmup()` then makes the causal and noncausal LSE calls when `enable_jit_warmup` is on, and none when it is off. They pass in the ROCm image against this commit's `rocm_aiter_fa.py`.

The small-model probes above used the ROCm image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-e68efc68...` (vLLM 0.32.1rc1), with the pre-rebase version of this commit's backend file overlaid. The commit was rebased onto current `main` afterwards. The unit tests were re-run on the rebased file. The serving runs below use this commit's `rocm_aiter_fa.py`.

### Serving

Same requests as [#67083](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67083), on MI355X, image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-f5d93296c8ec82b7e7dabdb308d24d43cb1907bf`. Both arms use this image. The patched arm uses this commit's `rocm_aiter_fa.py`. Weights are not loaded (`--load-format dummy`). `vllm bench serve`, random 1024 prompt and 512 output tokens, range ratio 0, `ignore_eos`, `num_warmups` 0, `request_rate` inf. c8 is 8 prompts, c32 is 32.

| Model | c8 | c32 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gemma-2-2b-it, TP1 | 1458 / 1462 | 546 / 4568 |
| Muse Spark MXFP4, TP8 | 625 / 617 | 433 / 1767 |

The c32 tok/s gap is not a steady-state speedup. With `--num-warmups 0`, the baseline's one-time module build (about 27 s) lands inside the timed c32 run, and this PR moves it to startup. TTFT is the metric to read; after the first extend, both arms run the same kernels.

On the patched arm, JIT warmup reports `AiterFlashAttentionExtendKernel (2 keys)`. Only `mha_varlen_fwd_bf16_…_mask_lse_…` is logged as built, because this image already ships `…_nmask_lse_…` (and `…_mask_nlse_…`) in its AITER prebuild; on a cold cache both LSE modules build, as in the small-model table above. commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep non-float all-reduces off AITER custom all-reduce
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With AITER custom all-reduce enabled (the default), `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` fails at TP>1 because the n-gram embedding all-reduces int8 tensors, which AITER's kernel rejects; this PR routes non-float all-reduces to PyNCCL, as vLLM's own custom all-reduce already does.

The FP8 MoE oracle fix landed in #66350. With it, this checkpoint gets past MoE selection and fails here instead.

## Validation

8x MI355X, `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-60bd6dd2edd175a1c55fd3488f871e4c3d2ef27d` (includes #66350), checkpoint revision `7fb48d70`. "This PR" is the same image with this diff applied.

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
    --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 256 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3
```

### Startup

| | main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TP2 | Triton FP8 MoE is selected, then the profile run fails with `RuntimeError: custom allreduce only supports float32, float16 and bfloat16` | Starts: Triton FP8 MoE, `['AITER_CUSTOM', 'PYNCCL']` all-reduce |

### Accuracy

GPQA-Diamond, thinking mode, mean of 8 repeats over the 198 questions, with this PR:

```bash
evalscope eval --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 --api-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions \
    --datasets gpqa_diamond --eval-batch-size 64 --repeats 8 \
    --generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95,"top_k":20,"max_tokens":131072,"timeout":7200}'
```

| | GPQA-Diamond |
| --- | --- |
| [Model card](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8) | 91.7 |
| This PR, TP2 | 92.3 |

EvalScope 1.14.1. All 1584 generations completed; the longest used 127k of the 131k token cap.

### Unit tests

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_rocm_aiter_custom_ar.py
```

| | Result on MI355X |
| --- | --- |
| main | 1 failed, 5 passed. The failure is the new int8 case |
| This PR | 6 passed |

`test_rocm_aiter_custom_allreduce[eager]` now also all-reduces an int8 tensor. It asserts that AITER declines it and that the result is correct.

## Details

The Qwen4Exp n-gram embedding all-reduces its FP8 rows as raw int8 bytes. Each row has a single owner, so the sum is exact. AITER's `should_custom_ar` accepts any dtype, but its kernel only supports float32, float16 and bfloat16. The wrapper now applies the same dtype check as vLLM's `CustomAllreduce.should_custom_ar`, so these tensors fall back to PyNCCL. Float all-reduces are unaffected.

commits.pr_title: [Doc] Make CUDA 13 the default in the GPU install guide
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

#62575 removed CUDA 12.9 from the release pipeline, so vLLM 0.32.0 is the last release with `cu129` wheels. The GPU install guide still named CUDA 12.9 as the default, and two of its install commands fail for vLLM 0.33.0. This PR makes CUDA 13 the default in the install steps and keeps the option to pick a CUDA variant.

## Claims

- `gpu.cuda.inc.md` names CUDA 13.0 as the release default and CUDA 13.2 as the nightly default.
- The `pip` step uses the PyTorch `cu130` index. The old `cu129` index has no `torch==2.14.0`, which vLLM 0.33.0 pins.
- The "specific CUDA version" step installs from `https://wheels.vllm.ai/<version>/<variant>` and reads the version from PyPI. The old step built a GitHub release asset URL from `releases/latest`, and that returns 404 today.
- A new note says that 0.32.0 is the last release with CUDA 12.9 wheels and shows how to install it.
- The nightly variant list and the contributing docs no longer use `cu129` as the current example.

## Validation

All resolutions use `uv 0.13.6 pip compile --python-version 3.12 --python-platform x86_64-manylinux_2_28`. Each new command resolves. Each old command fails, and that is the control.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| New snippet as written (PyPI version `0.33.0`, `CUDA_VARIANT=cu130`) | `vllm==0.33.0`, `torch==2.14.0+cu130` |
| New snippet with `VLLM_VERSION=0.32.0`, `CUDA_VARIANT=cu129` (the CUDA 12 note) | `vllm==0.32.0+cu129`, `torch==2.13.0+cu129` |
| Nightly, `--extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly --torch-backend=cu132` | `vllm==0.34.0rc1.dev460+g3d091b6f0`, `torch==2.14.0+cu132` |
| Control: `vllm==0.33.0` with `--torch-backend=cu129` (the old `pip` step) | fails: `there is no version of torch==2.14.0` |
| Control: `vllm==0.33.0` from `https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/cu129` | fails: same error |

The old "specific CUDA version" step fails for every variant. `releases/latest` returns the tag `v0.33.0rc3`, so the step requests `v0.33.0rc3/vllm-0.33.0rc3+cu130-...whl`. `cu130`, `cu132` and `cu129` all return 404. The `v0.32.0` `+cu129` asset returns 206, which proves that the probe works.

Facts behind the new text:

- `https://wheels.vllm.ai/0.33.0/` lists `cpu/`, `cu130/`, `vllm/` and `xpu/`. `0.33.0/cu129/` and `0.33.0/cu132/` return 404. `0.32.0/cu129/vllm/` serves `vllm-0.32.0+cu129` wheels for x86_64 and aarch64.
- `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` builds wheels with `CUDA_VERSION=12.9.1` and `13.0.2` at `v0.32.0`, with `13.0.2` only at `v0.33.0`, and with `13.2.1` on `main`. `VLLM_MAIN_CUDA_VERSION` defaults to `"13.0"` at `v0.33.0` and to `"13.2"` on `main` (`vllm/envs.py`).
- `https://wheels.vllm.ai/nightly/vllm/` and `nightly/cu132/vllm/` serve the same `dev460+g3d091b6f0` wheels. `nightly/cu130/` stops at `dev156` and `nightly/cu129/` stops at `0.32.0rc1.dev100`. `nightly/cpu/` and `nightly/xpu/` serve `dev398` wheels.
- PyPI `torch==2.14.0` requires `cuda-toolkit==13.0.3`.

`pre-commit run --files` on the three changed files passes, including `typos` and `markdownlint-cli2`. I did not build the docs site, and I did not run the `pip` command.

## Details

- The new snippet uses the per-release index on `wheels.vllm.ai` instead of a GitHub asset URL. The default variant has no `+cuXXX` suffix, so a URL template fails for the default variant. If later releases add more CUDA variants, the same command works with a new `CUDA_VARIANT`.
- Out of scope: `setup.py` `detect_system_cuda_variant` still maps CUDA 12 PyTorch to `cu129`, so `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` cannot find a wheel for new commits on a CUDA 12 PyTorch. #62575 named this as a follow-up.
- Out of scope: the wheel steps in `.buildkite/release-pipeline.yaml` on `main` keep the label "CUDA 13.0" but build with `CUDA_VERSION=13.2.1`.
- Duplicate check. These open PRs edit the same section, but none of them makes CUDA 13 the default after the 12.9 drop:
    - #47628 changes the default to 13.0 but keeps 12.9 as a current variant. It has merge conflicts and no update since 2026-10-17.
    - #50822 moves the variant install to the wheel index but keeps 12.9 as the default.
    - #57612 adds nightly `cu129` instructions.
    - #61283 is a wheel-tagging change. Its version of this snippet still builds a `+cu${CUDA_VERSION}` asset name from `releases/latest`. This PR conflicts with that hunk.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Avoid MIOpen's split-K conv solver in batch-invariant mode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On ROCm 10.0, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` does not hold for models whose vision encoders run certain forward convolutions, such as Unlimited-OCR-2 and DeepSeek-OCR, because MIOpen picks a split-K solver that accumulates with atomics. This makes `test_unlimited_ocr2_excess_markers_survive_preemption[ROCM_AITER_FA]` flaky on MI355 even after the DASH routing fix in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68563. **This is a temporary workaround.** It disables that solver in batch-invariant mode. It should be reverted for `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` once the ROCm base image is on ROCm 10.3.

## Claims

- Fixes the remaining flakiness in `test_unlimited_ocr2_excess_markers_survive_preemption[ROCM_AITER_FA]` on MI355. On `main` it failed 1 of 8 runs; with this change it passed 17 of 17.
- Makes DeepSeek-OCR batch invariant on ROCm. On `main`, solo and batched outputs differed in 12 of 12 comparisons; with this change all 12 are bit-identical.
- Changes behavior only on ROCm with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`.

## Validation

bad = 0

Standalone MIOpen reproducer: 200 repeated calls of the encoder's 512→1024, 3×3, stride-2 bf16 convolution on a 1×512×32×32 input, compared with the first call.

<details>
<summary>Script and output</summary>

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(1, 512, 32, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
w = torch.randn(1024, 512, 3, 3, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
b = torch.randn(1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
ref = F.conv2d(x, w, b, stride=2, padding=1)
diffs = sum(bool((F.conv2d(x, w, b, stride=2, padding=1) != ref).any()) for _ in range(200))
print("RESULT", diffs, "of 200 differ")
```

| Environment | MIOpen solver | Result |
|---|---|---|
| ROCm 10.0, default | `ConvAsmImplicitGemmGTCDynamicFwdXdlopsNHWC` (`..._gkgs`) | 200 of 200 differ |
| ROCm 10.0, `MIOPEN_DEBUG_CONV_IMPLICIT_GEMM_ASM_FWD_GTC_XDLOPS_NHWC=0` | `ConvHipImplicitGemmGroupFwdXdlops` | 0 of 200 differ |
| ROCm 10.0, `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` | none | `No suitable algorithm was found to execute the required convolution` |
| ROCm 10.3 (`2.16.0a0+rocm10.3.0a20261110`), `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` | `GemmFwdRest` | 0 of 200 differ |

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** For the Unlimited-OCR-2 encoder's 512→1024, 3×3, stride-2 convolution, MIOpen's find step on ROCm 10.0 selects `ConvAsmImplicitGemmGTCDynamicFwdXdlopsNHWC` with a GEMM-K global split (`gkgs`) kernel. The split partial sums are combined with atomic adds, so the result depends on execution order. MIOpen runs the find step once and reuses the same solver for every call, so the nondeterminism is inside the kernel, not in algorithm selection. The drift in image embeddings accumulates over the test's 192 forced tokens and can exceed the 0.5 logit tolerance.

**Why not `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic`.** That is the intended control, and the right long-term fix is for batch-invariant mode to set it. On ROCm 10.0, MIOpen's forward implicit-GEMM solvers reject deterministic mode outright, so these convolutions fail with `No suitable algorithm was found`. On ROCm 10.3, deterministic mode finds a valid solver for the same convolution. https://github.com/ROCm/rocm-libraries/pull/14508 is one related fix in that range; it enables the CK grouped forward solvers in deterministic mode.

**Workaround.** `override_envs_for_invariance` already sets environment variables for batch-invariant mode, and on ROCm it now also sets `MIOPEN_DEBUG_CONV_IMPLICIT_GEMM_ASM_FWD_GTC_XDLOPS_NHWC=0`. MIOpen then falls back to `ConvHipImplicitGemmGroupFwdXdlops`, which does not use split-K. Its standalone benchmark time was within 2% of the disabled solver (0.0751 ms against 0.0738 ms).

**Limitations.**
- This disables only the solver that was observed to be nondeterministic. Other shapes could still select a different nondeterministic solver until batch-invariant mode requests determinism directly.
- Validation covered Unlimited-OCR-2 and DeepSeek-OCR. Other models with convolutions were not swept, but the change only removes one candidate from MIOpen's find step.
- The follow-up, which replaces this environment variable with `torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True` once the ROCm base image is on 10.3, is marked with a `TODO` in the code. It has not been validated end to end, because no vLLM image on ROCm 10.3 was available.
- `pre-commit` passed, except `mypy`. It was skipped locally because the host Python is 3.10, which cannot parse an unrelated file.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Read /v1/decisions predicates like /v1/systemone noul questions
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`/v1/decisions` reads a `predicate` question as a lettered choice (`A: false`, `B: true`), while `/v1/systemone` reads the same yes/no question (`noul`) with bare `yes` / `no` labels. As a result, one question can get very different answers from the two endpoints on the same server. This PR builds a predicate's read with the same `build_question(..., "noul", ...)` call that `/v1/systemone` uses. Fixes #68914.

## Claims

- A `predicate` on `/v1/decisions` now gets the same prompt, labels and probability as a `noul` question with the same instructions on `/v1/systemone`, for every read strategy.
- Qwen3-0.6B, "Is an action requested?" on "My card was charged twice.": the predicate probability goes from 0.5 (an exact tie between the `A` and `B` logprobs in bf16) to 0.99974, which matches `/v1/systemone` noul.
- The response format is unchanged: `probability` is still the probability of "true" / "yes".

## Validation

All runs on one H200 at main bdcf4258 with this diff applied, using the precompiled wheel.

Unit tests (`test_decisions.py` and `test_slot_strategy.py`; one test updated, `test_predicate_reads_like_a_systemone_noul_question` added):

```
41 passed in 7.41s
```

Full decisions suites (`pytest -q tests/entrypoints/openai/decisions tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions`):

```
182 passed in 436.55s
```

End to end, `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --max-model-len 4096`, with the same request 3 times:

| | main bf16 | this PR bf16 | main fp32 | this PR fp32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/v1/decisions` predicate | 0.5 | 0.99974 | 0.52688 | 0.99979 |
| `/v1/systemone` noul | 0.99974 | 0.99974 | 0.99979 | 0.99979 |

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/decisions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","input":"My card was charged twice.","questions":[{"type":"predicate","instructions":"Is an action requested?"}]}'
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/systemone -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B","state":"My card was charged twice.","questions":{"q":{"type":"noul","instructions":"Is an action requested?"}}}'
```

## Details

Root cause: `make_read_question` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions/adapters.py`) mapped `PredicateQuestion` to a `ChoiceQuestion` read with options `false` / `true` under the labels `A` / `B`. On Qwen3-0.6B, the first-token logprobs on that prompt are `A` -0.714713 and `B` -0.714713 in bf16, so the result is exactly 0.5. On the noul prompt, `yes` is -0.0016.

Strategies with trained prompts handle noul on their own terms (slot models render `yes`/`no` with the trained descriptions; joint-schema and D3 models have a dedicated noul input). Before this change, those strategies were given a two-option choice named `false` / `true` instead. Building the read through `build_question` gives every strategy exactly what `/v1/systemone` gives it, and also applies the same `max_options` check. A noul read lists `yes` first, so the predicate's probability is now `probs[0]`.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor] Use `FULL` instead of `NONE` during MR V2 full-graph capture
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Use `FULL` instead of `NONE` during MR V2 full-graph capture.

Use a scoped wrapper bypass to separate graph mode from capture ownership, and propagate the mode to DBO microbatches. Preserve eager warmup and PIECEWISE behavior.

Previously, downstream code needed a V2-specific fallback:

```
# V2 captures FULL graphs with runtime mode NONE.
if context.cudagraph_runtime_mode != CUDAGraphMode.FULL and not (
    context.cudagraph_runtime_mode == CUDAGraphMode.NONE
    and torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
):
    return None
```
Now


```py
if context.cudagraph_runtime_mode != CUDAGraphMode.FULL:
    return None
```

## Test

Covered in current unit test

commits.pr_title: [feat] Add Omni support to the Transformers backend
commits.pr_body:
### What does this PR do? cc: @hmellor → **This PR makes the Transformers modeling backend serve Omni models, with audio, image, and video supported in a single request.** I've tried to scope the work as much as I could, but there are a lot of edge cases, such as which audio a fused `use_audio_in_video` span should pair with, bidirectional encoders sitting inside multimodal configs, and one quantity carrying three different names across the Qwen family, that we need to handle to fully cover these models. Some of these challenges may also warrant a broader design discussion upstream around a more standardized upstream interface. → Requires Transformers 5.23.0: https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49437 shipped in 5.21 and https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49435 is merged for 5.23.0. Until the `transformers` pin allows 5.23.0, the Omni tests in `processing/test_transformers_omni.py` will fail on CI. ### Notes on each evaluated model family Ultimately, I decided against pushing anything I couldn't evaluate locally, and evaluated all Omni-model families, on 1× NVIDIA L4 (22 GiB) where they could run at all; 4/10 are served on the Transformers backend with HF parity, 2/10 only partly, and 4/10 could not be, two of them because I found no usable checkpoint that's on the Hub and two because of backend gaps that are separate, out-of-scope work.
Essential Notes on Each Evaluated Model Family
[Qwen2.5-Omni-3B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-3B) ✅ → Audio, Video, Image → Logprobs match HF Transformers 🤗 [gemma-3n-E2B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-3n-E2B-it) ✅ → Audio, Image (No video tower in the family) → Logprobs match HF Transformers 🤗 [gemma-4-E2B-it](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E2B-it) ✅ → Audio, Video, Image → Logprobs match HF Transformers 🤗 [gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct](https://huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct) ✅ → Audio, Image → 90 of 90 exact greedy tokens against HF, but not verified in the test suite because vLLM runs the 9.56 GiB checkpoint natively as w4a16 while HF decompresses it to bf16 at load, about 24 GiB for 12B parameters, which exceeds the L4's 22 GiB, so the reference had to run on CPU 👀 [Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct) 👀 → Audio, Video, Image → GPU poor 💪 (parity not measurable on 22 GiB). Initializes and passes the processing suite, but the bf16 checkpoint is 65.7 GiB, and the 19.06 GiB AWQ one gets to 21.86 GiB in use and OOMs 222 MiB short of 22.04. I found other smaller community variants that are either untrained or expert-pruned into gibberish → Known gap: Two audios of different lengths in one request give the shorter one a placeholder one token longer than its features produce (27 vs 26). This predates the PR, since on main the same item's mask already disagrees with its features [embeddinggemma-2](https://huggingface.co/google/embeddinggemma-2) 👀 → Audio, Image, Text → Separate backend work: `embeddinggemma-2` is a bidirectional encoder but the backend currently treats it as causal because it is multimodal; so its embeddings diverge from HF Transformers, cosine 0.844 to 0.906 and 0.9999 once the reference is forced causal. [phi-4-audio](https://huggingface.co/JacobLinCool/phi-4-audio) ❌ → None served → No usable checkpoint: Every real-weight one I found is the legacy remote-code format, and the only real-weight one on the native architecture has its whole vision tower removed. The converter exists upstream, but no converted checkpoint has been published. [pe-av-small](https://huggingface.co/facebook/pe-av-small) ❌ → None served → Separate backend work: It has no `get_input_embeddings` override, and its ModernBERT text tower hits the same attention issue as `embeddinggemma-2`. [Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Nemotron-3-Nano-Omni-30B-A3B-Reasoning-NVFP4) ❌ → None served → No usable checkpoint: → Every checkpoint I found uses a different architecture from Transformers' own implementation, with different config and weight names. Only 1 of 7,349 weight names overlaps, and there is no converter to bridge the two. [Inkling-0.6B-A0.6B](https://huggingface.co/inference-optimization/Inkling-0.6B-A0.6B) ❌ → None served → Separate backend work: Its `mlp.w13_dn` weight needs `Interleave(dim=0)` then `Chunk(dim=0)` which the concatenating `orig_to_new_stacked` cannot express.
Known limitations
→ use_audio_in_video: Server-level only (`--mm-processor-kwargs`); a per-request value raises, unlike native Qwen-Omni and `examples/offline_inference/qwen2_5_omni/only_thinker.py`. Fused mode follows native: One audio per video, no mixing with standalone audio, and the processor cache is skipped → Fused mode coverage: Processing tests only, no generation test; video-only profiling in fused mode raises, as in native → gemma-3n newlines: A newline right before a placeholder is spliced as `\n` + `\n\n` where HF merges `\n\n\n`; this backend-wide behaviour predates the PR, and the processing test marks it `xfail(strict=True)` → gemma-4 short videos: Clips under 32 frames fail when frames are sampled, because the video processor defaults to `num_frames=32` → Pipeline parallelism: Untested; gemma-3n/4 per-layer inputs don't cross ranks yet
Changes outside the Omni path
→ Video log: `_is_video_model` now asks users to report to Transformers, as you asked on #57441 → RMSNorm fuser: Skips norms that don't mean over the last dim, which gemma-3n's MobileNetV5 (`RmsNorm2d`) needs → Ignored weights: A `_keys_to_ignore_on_load_unexpected` match is kept when the model has a parameter for it, which gemma-4's vision tower needs → Gemma 3 boi branch: Removed; dead since v5.16.1 and wrong for gemma-3n → M-RoPE attention mask: `get_rope_index` gets an all-ones `attention_mask` wherever it takes one, for Qwen-Omni's text-only path; positions are unchanged for Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen3-VL and GLM-4V
### Testing
Commands and results (1× L4, Transformers main)
→ `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_omni.py`: 11 passed, 1 xfailed (gemma-3n, see Known limitations) → `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_transformers_{audio,image,video}.py`: 38 passed, 2 xfailed (the upstream Emu3 and Voxtral xfails) → `pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k test_processing_correctness_transformers`: 9 passed → `pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_transformers_omni.py`, one model per run: Qwen2.5-Omni-3B, gemma-3n-E2B-it and gemma-4-E2B-it pass HF logprob parity → gemma-4-E2B-it also passes HF parity with torch.compile on, and piecewise CUDA graph replay keeps its input addresses (checked with `VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG`) → `pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k `: 9 passed, 1 skipped; the 2 failures also fail on main here (Emu3 OOMs on 22 GiB since #56492, and a stale `grouped_topk` kernel in my build) → `pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py`: 34 passed, 2 skipped; the 5 failures also fail on main here (gated meta-llama, stale MLA and Marlin kernels in my build)

## Overview

Follow-up to #63205 (speculator config classes) and #65263 (Gemma-4 MTP prefix-cache fix). This replaces the remaining checks on the speculative method name and draft `model_type`, such as `use_eagle()`, `use_dspark()`, `method in (...)` and `use_gemma4_mtp()`. commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Store one copy of the offloaded indexer across TP ranks
commits.pr_body:
## What changes

With HiSparse and an `OffloadingConnector` (which offloads only the indexer cache) on a single node with TP > 1, the CPU tier now stores **one** copy of the indexer cache shared by all TP ranks, instead of one copy per rank. The bytes are identical on every rank, so at TP4 this cuts the tier's host memory by 4× for the same capacity.

Why it happened: the shared-copy layout requires every KV cache group to be TP-replicated. HiSparse's resident and hot GPU page groups are raw pages with no TP metadata, so the check always failed. Those groups are never offloaded, so the check now looks only at the groups that are.

Example config that is affected:
```bash
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[
    {"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":64}},
    {"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":4294967296}}]}}'
```
Before, the 4 GiB tier held 1 GiB worth of blocks (four copies). After, it holds the full 4 GiB.

#68771 adds `hisparse_config.host_pool_gib`, which splits one budget between the HiSparse pool and this tier. Whichever of the two PRs lands second will make that split count the tier's actual number of copies.

## Validation

`test_hisparse_indexer_tier_is_single_copy_under_tp` fails on `main` and passes here:
```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py
```
On 4×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4, TP4), with this change applied together with #68771, the indexer tier was a single shared region: `Created mmap file /dev/shm/vllm_offload_<engine>.mmap (4.05 GB)`. Prefix hits from the tier still worked: 3968/4000 cached tokens after 40 other 4000-token prompts.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model][Perf] Fold the k_out dequant and fp8 query quant into the QK-norm+RoPE+KV-cache fusion for ROCM_AITER_FA, ROCM_ATTN, and ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
This PR depends on: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6808, which has already made it into the most recently pinned aiter release for vLLM (0.1.29).

When this fusion and FP8 KV-Cache are active, there's an extra dequantize op (shown below) after the fused kernel to convert `k_out` from FP8 back to BF16 so the downstream attn pieces (ROCM_ATTN & ROCM_AITER_FA) can consume it properly. 
```bash
def convert_fp8(
    output: torch.Tensor, input: torch.Tensor, scale: float = 1.0, kv_dtype: str = "fp8"
) -> None:
    torch.ops._C_cache_ops.convert_fp8(output, input, scale, kv_dtype)
```
This extra small op launch overhead can be saved by folding the conversion portion back into the fused kernel, as it already has an option to output k_out in BF16 when FP8 KV Cache is active. We take `k_out` via `k_out_unquantized`. 

As for the FP8 query quant, it follows the same idea; we fold the FP8 quantization portion back into the fused kernel. `ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN` consumes quantized q_out_fp8; we're only able to fold the extra quantize op if the method is `per_tensor` and one corner case of `per-head` (if we have only one local KV head, we'd only need 1 scale). If we have more than 1 local KV head, it falls back to an extra ` static_scaled_fp8_quant` launch to take care of the quantization. 

To be able to fold all query quantization cases back into the fused kernel, this requires further kernel-side changes within AITER; it needs to take in a scale tensor of size [num_kv_heads] and have the kernel pick the scale for each Q head. I digress; this could be a favorable follow-up PR later on, topic for another day :). 

## Validation

Setup: 1x MI350 (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2, AITER main @ e9f7b55. Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B at TP1 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`. Base is `main` @ 98468d0, with the fusion enabled on both sides. Runs alternated between the base and the new model over 2 rounds × 3 repeats.

| Backend | Base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| ROCM_AITER_FA | 0.8954 | 0.8946 |
| ROCM_ATTN | 0.8817 | 0.8832 |
| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | 0.8939 | 0.8893 |

| ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN | 4.80 → 4.66 (-2.9%) | 6.66 → 6.65 | 10.87 → 10.51 | 13.56 → 13.56 |

**Unit tests**

    # 2073 passed

**Reproduce**

    VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
      --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Give apt a longer retry window in ROCm image builds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

A deadsnakes PPA 503 that outlasted apt's default retries failed a from-scratch ROCm base image build ([Buildkite #103973](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103973), `Ensure ROCm stack + runtime`). This gives apt a longer retry window in the ROCm images.

**Split:** the `build.sh` half (exit 75 and a step retry when a mirror still fails after apt's retries) moved to #68829, so this PR no longer changes `build.sh` and can be cached with `/ci rocm cache`.

## Claims

- apt rides out mirror outages of up to about 5 minutes per package (it used to give up after about 100 s).
- The runtime image's apt step (`docker/Dockerfile.rocm`) no longer passes `-o Acquire::Retries=3`, which overrode the stack image's config, so it gets the same window. This changes the runtime key (`Kr`).

## Validation

- `apt-config` parses the new `80-retries` file. The backoff is 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, then 60 s ×4, about 303 s per package.
- In [#103973 attempt 2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103973#01a1f04a-56c0-43a1-b6ec-598ef347b5d8) apt retried each failed `.deb` 3 times (the `Ign:` lines) over about 100 s before `E: Failed to fetch .../python3.14_3.14.10-1+jammy1_amd64.deb 503 Service Unavailable`.
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files is clean.

## Details

**apt.** jammy's apt 2.4 already treats 408/429/500/502/503/504/599 as transient (`methods/basehttp.cc`) and retries `Acquire::Retries` times (default 3) with exponential backoff (`apt-pkg/acquire-worker.cc`). `80-retries` raises this to 10 retries, with the backoff capped at 60 s. It is written in the `base` stage, which every other stage builds from, in both `Dockerfile.rocm_base` and `Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250`. That is intended: the file is inherited by the stack, runtime, test and release images, and `Dockerfile.rocm`'s apt step now relies on it instead of `-o Acquire::Retries=3` (a command-line `-o` overrides `apt.conf.d`). `Dockerfile.rocm_gfx1250` keeps its explicit `Retries=3`: it wraps that apt step in `timeout --kill-after=30s 5m`, so a longer retry window would only run into that bound.

**The AITER prebuild failure** in #103973 attempt 1 happened about 2.4 h into `PREBUILD_KERNELS=1 python3 setup.py bdist_wheel` (AITER v0.1.29, Python 3.14). Ninja jobs [308]-[317] of `module_gemm_a8w8` all failed together with ENOENT in two unrelated directories, `/tmp` and the module's build directory. Jobs [1]-[307] had succeeded. Creating a file in a directory that exists cannot return ENOENT, so those directories were gone. I read AITER v0.1.29's prebuild path:
- the build directory is removed only once, before the CK thread pool starts;
- `clear_build` runs only under `AITER_REBUILD`;
- the `FileBaton` locks use PID-based stale detection, which can never fire between threads of one process;
- nothing touches `/tmp`.

The same step succeeded in a Python 3.14 build on Nov 13 (#102331, about 10,180 s), so the fault looks external (host, buildkit or overlay storage). Neither PR retries it. If it recurs, the next step is to capture the builder's storage state (buildkitd logs, `docker buildx du`, disk usage) on failure and find the actual cause before matching on it.

**Limits:** this alone does not retry the step when an outage outlasts the ~5 min window; #68829 adds that. This PR changes `Dockerfile.rocm_base` and `Dockerfile.rocm`, so its own CI rebuilds the base and runtime images; run `/ci rocm cache` once that CI passes.

No open PR changes apt retries (searched `Acquire::Retries rocm`, `rocm base apt retry`, `deadsnakes 503`).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Emit the prefill staging plan without a dense prefill backend
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #68668, the "known gap" follow-up from #61243.

## Problem

HiSparse on GLM-5.3-Flash fails at the first prefill with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`. The model is NoPE (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`), so `FlashMLASparseImpl` drops the dense-MHA prefill path and the layer ends up with `prefill_backend=None`. The metadata builder then skips `SparseMLAPrefillMetadata` entirely, but the HiSparse MQA prefill path stages through its `host_staging_plan`, and `HiSparseMLAIndexGroup._prefill_gather_plan` asserts on it.

## Fix

Build the prefill metadata when HiSparse is active even if the layer has no dense-MHA prefill backend, and skip `prepare_metadata` when there is no backend. The route stays `SPARSE_MQA`, so no dense-prefill path is selected; the MQA path just gets the staging plan it already requires. Behavior is unchanged when a prefill backend exists or HiSparse is off.

## Testing

- New test `test_hisparse_prefill_staging_plan_without_dense_prefill_backend` in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py`: real `SparseMLACommonMetadataBuilder` for a NoPE `fp8_ds_mla` + HiSparse config with `prefill_backend=None`; asserts the prefill metadata, the `SPARSE_MQA` route and the host staging plan (staged rows, miss mask, remapped block table).
- `pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k test_hisparse_prefill_staging_plan_without_dense_prefill_backend` (H100 attention job; the test module is CUDA/ROCm/XPU-gated).
- Fail-first: with the fix reverted the same flow fails with `AssertionError` on `assert metadata.prefill is not None`, the precondition of the reported assertion; patched it passes. The test module cannot run on a CPU-only machine, so that check ran as a CPU mirror of the test using the real builder and staging-plan code, substituting only the triton token-mapping kernel.
- No model-eval impact: the new branch only fires when HiSparse is on and the layer has no prefill backend, a configuration that previously crashed.

No other open PR covers this (checked for #68668 and the staging-plan area before starting). AI assistance was used for this change.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Hoist `additional_tools` input items into Responses tools
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Codex (>= 0.169) declares its tools through an `additional_tools` item in the Responses `input` list instead of the top-level `tools` field. vLLM rejects every such request with `400 Unsupported input item type: additional_tools`, so Codex cannot talk to vLLM at all. This PR moves the tools of those items into `request.tools` when the request is validated.

## Claims

- Responses requests carrying `additional_tools` input items no longer fail with a 400; their tools are offered to the model exactly like top-level `tools` (appended after them, in input order).
- Hoisted tools go through the same request validation as top-level ones: `tool_choice` stays `auto` (instead of being forced to `none` for a request with no top-level `tools`), `required` and named choices resolve against them, and grammar-format custom tools are still refused.
- An `additional_tools` item whose `tools` is not a list is refused with a clean 400 (`parameter=input`).
- No behavior change for requests without `additional_tools` items.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** A real Codex Desktop 0.169.1 request (from a session rollout) replayed through `ResponsesRequest` validation, `construct_input_messages` and `construct_tool_dicts`, i.e. the path that raised the error:

```text

FAILED: VLLMValidationError: Unsupported input item type: additional_tools (parameter=input)

# this PR
OK
tool_choice: auto
message roles: ['developer', 'user']
request.tools: [('namespace', 'functions'), ('namespace', 'clock'), ('namespace', 'collaboration'), ('namespace', 'mcp__cua_repl')]

```

**New unit tests fail before and pass after.**

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py -k additional_tools
```

```text
# base commit
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_item_hoisted_into_tools
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_items_merged_without_top_level_tools
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_satisfy_tool_choice[required-required]
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_satisfy_tool_choice[tool_choice1-clock__sleep]
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_custom_grammar_rejected
FAILED tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py::test_additional_tools_item_without_tools_list_rejected
6 failed, 11 deselected

# this PR
6 passed, 11 deselected
```

**No regressions** in the offline Responses unit tests (`test_protocol.py`, `test_responses_utils.py`, `test_function_call_parsing.py`, `test_response_input_to_harmony.py`, `test_serving_responses.py`, `test_streaming_events.py`, `test_parsable_context_unit.py`, `test_errors.py`, `test_sampling_params.py`): all pass. `pre-commit run` passes on the changed files.

**End to end.** `test_namespace_tool_from_additional_tools_item` (in `test_namespace_tool_separator.py`, `RemoteOpenAIServer` + `Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B`) sends the namespace tool only through an `additional_tools` item and asserts the namespaced function call. It runs in the existing `entrypoints/openai/responses` CI step. GPU validation against a served model: _TODO, pending_.

## Details

**Root cause.** `additional_tools` is a Responses item type (`AdditionalTools` in openai-python: `role: "developer"`, `tools: list[Tool]`). vLLM's input conversion (`_construct_message_from_response_item`) has no branch for it, so the item falls through to the final `raise VLLMValidationError("Unsupported input item type: ...")` (a 400 since #55974).

**Fix.** A `mode="before"` validator on `ResponsesRequest` (`hoist_additional_tools_items`) removes `additional_tools` items from `input` and appends their tools to `tools`. Doing it once at the request boundary means every consumer of `request.tools` (tool rendering, tool parser, tool-call name mapping, streaming processor, harmony path) sees them without per-site changes. Skipping the item instead would silently remove all of Codex's tools.

The validator is defined last in `ResponsesRequest` on purpose. Pydantic runs `before` model validators in reverse definition order, so it runs ahead of `check_tool_usage` and `check_custom_tool_format`. Placed earlier, `check_tool_usage` would see no `tools` and rewrite `tool_choice="auto"` to `"none"`, so the 400 would disappear but the model would never call a tool. `test_additional_tools_items_merged_without_top_level_tools` and `test_additional_tools_satisfy_tool_choice` pin this.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**

- The tools are rendered with the other tools at the start of the prompt rather than at the item's position in the conversation. That matches how chat templates render tools, and Codex sends the item ahead of the conversation. A client that adds tools mid-session changes the rendered tool block, so the prompt prefix (and its prefix-cache hit) changes from that turn on.
- With `previous_response_id`, vLLM replays stored messages but not tools, as it already does for top-level `tools`, so a chained request must resend its `additional_tools` items. Codex sends `store: false` with the full history, so it is unaffected.

**Limitation (separate issue).** Codex also sends a *custom* tool inside a namespace (`functions.exec`). `get_function_tools` keeps only `function` entries of a namespace, so that tool is still not shown to the model (it is absent from the list above). That gap exists for top-level namespace tools too and is left to a follow-up.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Voxtral: drop the unused model field from TranscriptionRequest
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Voxtral and Voxtral Realtime pass `model=model_config.model` to mistral-common's `TranscriptionRequest` when they build the transcription prompt. mistral-common does not read this field when it encodes a transcription, and mistralai/mistral-common#455 proposes to deprecate it. This PR drops the unused model field.

## Claims

- The transcription prompts do not change: both models produce the same prompt token ids as before.
- With mistral-common#455 installed, building these prompts no longer emits its request-field `DeprecationWarning`.
- mistral-common request models forbid extra fields (`extra="forbid"`), so a mistral-common release without the field would reject this call. After this PR, Voxtral no longer sets it.

## Validation

The reproducer below builds a real `ModelConfig` (`tokenizer_mode="mistral"`, `config_format="mistral"`, tokenizer and config only, no weights) for each model. It calls `get_generation_prompt` on 1 s of silence with `language="en"` and records the warnings.

| mistral-common | main (79897d9f4) | this PR |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1.13.0 and 1.13.1 | Voxtral: 383 ids, Realtime: 39 ids, no warning | identical ids (same sha1), no warning |
| #455 head (aaf3f88) | `DeprecationWarning` at `voxtral.py:462` and `voxtral_realtime.py:515` | identical ids, no warning |

```
# main, mistral-common at #455
VoxtralForConditionalGeneration prompt ids: 383 3367b3df4157 deprecation warnings: ['vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral.py:462']
VoxtralRealtimeGeneration prompt ids: 39 de4ddfd5a796 deprecation warnings: ['vllm/model_executor/models/voxtral_realtime.py:515']
# this PR, mistral-common at #455
VoxtralForConditionalGeneration prompt ids: 383 3367b3df4157 deprecation warnings: []
VoxtralRealtimeGeneration prompt ids: 39 de4ddfd5a796 deprecation warnings: []
```

<details>
<summary>Reproducer</summary>

```python
import hashlib
import warnings

import mistral_common.deprecation as deprecation
import numpy as np

from vllm.config import ModelConfig
from vllm.config.speech_to_text import SpeechToTextConfig, SpeechToTextParams
from vllm.model_executor.models.voxtral import VoxtralForConditionalGeneration
from vllm.model_executor.models.voxtral_realtime import VoxtralRealtimeGeneration

for model, cls in [
    ("mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507", VoxtralForConditionalGeneration),
    ("mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-4B-Realtime-2602", VoxtralRealtimeGeneration),
]:
    config = ModelConfig(model, tokenizer_mode="mistral", config_format="mistral")
    # mistral-common#455 warns once per process; reset so each model reports.
    getattr(deprecation, "_warned_keys", set()).clear()
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        prompt = cls.get_generation_prompt(
            SpeechToTextParams(
                audio=np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.float32),
                stt_config=SpeechToTextConfig(),
                model_config=config,
                language="en",
            )
        )
    ids = prompt["prompt_token_ids"]
    deprecated = [
        f"{w.filename.split('vllm/', 1)[-1]}:{w.lineno}"
        for w in caught
        if issubclass(w.category, DeprecationWarning)
        and "request fields are deprecated" in str(w.message)
    ]
    print(cls.__name__, "prompt ids:", len(ids),
          hashlib.sha1(str(ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:12],
          "deprecation warnings:", deprecated)
```

</details>

`pre-commit run --files` on both files: passed.

Not run: GPU end-to-end transcription. The prompt ids are identical, so the model input does not change. CI's Speech to Text step runs a `mistralai/Voxtral-Mini-3B-2507` transcription end to end (`tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_transcription_validation.py::test_basic_audio`). If a mistral-common release removes the field before this change, that step fails end to end.

## Details

**Root cause.** Both `get_generation_prompt` implementations set `TranscriptionRequest.model` to the served model name. `encode_transcription` only reads the audio, the language and, for Realtime, the streaming mode, so the field has no effect.

**Fix.** Drop `model=`. The field is optional on every mistral-common version vLLM supports (`>= 1.13.0`), so the change needs no version check. No other vLLM code sets a request field that #455 deprecates.

**Tests.** No new test. With a released mistral-common, the field has no observable effect through real objects. A test would have to stub the tokenizer to inspect the request, which `tests/AGENTS.md` rules out. A test that turns warnings into errors would pass on main until mistral-common ships the deprecation.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Reject stop strings when the generate server has no tokenizer
commits.pr_body:
## Overview
  
Reject stop strings on the generate (token-in-token-out) route when the server has no tokenizer, instead of silently ignoring them.

## Claims

- `--skip-tokenizer-init` without `--tokens-only` now returns a `400` for stop strings. Before, it accepted them and never applied them.
- `--tokens-only` behaves as before.
- The Rust frontend already did this. Added a test  to maintain parity.

## Validation

```bash
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-server generate_rejects_stop_strings_without_tokenizer
# test routes::tests::generate_rejects_stop_strings_without_tokenizer ... ok
# test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 732 filtered out; finished in 0.05s
```

Python: `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_stop_strings_rejected_without_tokenizer`, now parametrized over `--tokens-only` and `--skip-tokenizer-init`. 

## Details

The `400` only fired when `force_no_detokenize` was set which is only true for `--tokens-only`. With plain `--skip-tokenizer-init`, `detokenize` stays `True`, there's no tokenizer and the detokenizer falls back to the base class, so stop strings went through and never matched. The check now uses `has_tokenizer`, which already covers both cases. The error message names both flags.

Not a duplicate of #46310: that one adds the check in `SamplingParams.verify()` for all entrypoints. This one only touches the generate route, next to the existing `bad_words` and `output_mode` tokenizer checks (#67408, #58588). Happy to drop this if the `verify()` approach lands first.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Give EngineCore the cleanup grace window when shutdown has no budget
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`AsyncLLM.shutdown()` and `LLM` teardown pass `timeout=None` to the EngineCore process manager. `get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout()` only applied the ROCm cleanup window (15 s, or `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`) when the budget was `0`, so `None` fell through to the generic 5 s. EngineCore and its workers were then SIGKILLed while EngineCore was still waiting for its workers to exit. This treats `None` like `0`. It also drops a leftover `fork` override in the hidden-state extraction test. Follows #52281, which added the window for the zero budget.

## Claims

- When an explicit shutdown with no request-drain budget takes longer than 5 s, EngineCore and its workers now get the cleanup window instead of `kill_process_tree`. That is 15 s on ROCm, or `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` if set.
- Other cases are unchanged: non-ROCm with the env var unset, a positive request timeout (the drain deadline stays exact), and explicit positive budgets.
- `test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model` runs its engine under the environment's start method (`spawn` in ROCm CI) instead of forcing `fork`.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** DP=2 (`mp`) `AsyncLLM` on Qwen3-0.6B, run as create, generate, `shutdown()`, 20 times, on MI355X with `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30` as in AMD CI. Workers on this host exit in about 1.5 s, so a test-only `sitecustomize` hook (`SLOW_WORKER_EXIT=8`) delays `WorkerProc.shutdown` by 8 s to match the slow ROCm teardowns seen in CI.

| 20 shutdowns | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `force killing remaining process EngineCore_DP*` | **40/40** | **0** |
| Workers force-killed | 40 | 0 |
| `Executor: all workers exited gracefully` | 0 | 40 |
| Median shutdown | 5.5 s (killed at the 5 s mark) | 9.6 s (workers finish exiting) |

The `main` log shows SIGTERM at 01:57:32 and `force killing remaining process EngineCore_DP0` at 01:57:37. That matches CI: in nightly [#103780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103780), `amd-distributed-dp-tests-*` and `amd-batch-invariance-distributed-4xh100` force-kill EngineCore exactly 5 s after SIGTERM, while workers that exit gracefully there take 5.0-5.3 s. Without the hook (workers exit in about 1.5 s), 5 shutdowns per side took the same about 1.5 s with no kills on either. So a healthy teardown is not slowed.

**Tests**

- `tests/v1/engine/test_startup_watch_processes.py`: 26 passed, 20 runs. The new `None` rows (ROCm → 15.0, env → 30.0) fail on `main`. The added rows pin the unchanged cases: non-ROCm `None` and positive request timeout with `None`.
- `test_extraction.py::test_extract_hidden_states_with_predictable_dummy_model` with `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn`: 20/20 passed.
- `v1/distributed/test_async_llm_dp.py -k "not ray"` (TP=1, DP=2): identical on `main` and this PR, 18 passed and 7 failed. The 7 failures are the same on both; they come from a `CacheConfig` `bool_parsing` validation error on the tiny-Llama cases, before any engine starts.
- `pre-commit run` (including mypy) is clean.

## Details

`get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout(request_timeout, process_timeout)` now returns the cleanup window when `request_timeout == 0 and process_timeout in (0, None)`. #52281 kept `None` unchanged only to limit its scope: `None` means "no outer budget". It is not a remaining budget that must be honoured, unlike an exhausted `0` that came from a positive drain timeout.

**Side effect:** every caller that passes `None` now waits up to 15 s on ROCm, or the env value, before force-killing a hung or failed EngineCore. Those callers are the `CoreEngineProcManager` startup-failure path, the liveness monitor after an engine dies, and headless/multi-API-server serve. Engines that exit promptly are unaffected.

**Not covered:** the sync finalizer path (`BackgroundResources.__call__`) passes `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, which defaults to 5. That value is neither `0` nor `None`, so it is unchanged.

**The test change.** `VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=fork` in `test_extraction.py` predates #49218, after which the test is spawn-safe. The override beats the `spawn` that ROCm CI's kernel-launch recorder sets. A fork child that loads GPU code after the parent initialised the profiler SDK can't be recorded (`# error=gpu_use_after_fork`), so `amd-extract-hidden-states-integration` never had a usable row in the [CI selector](https://ci.vllm.ai/selector)'s ROCm kernel table.

**Duplicate check.** No open PR changes `get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout` or this test (searched `get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout`, `force killing remaining process EngineCore`, `extract_hidden_states fork`). #50529, #54553 and #61562 touch other shutdown code.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Retry ROCm image builds when a package mirror still fails after apt's retries
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Split from #68527 so that PR stays cacheable with `/ci rocm cache`; the bot refuses to cache any PR that changes `build.sh`. #68527 keeps the Dockerfile half (a longer apt retry window). This PR is the `build.sh` half: when a ROCm image bake fails because a package mirror still returns 408/429/5xx after apt's own retries, `build.sh` exits 75 instead of 1, and the steps retry once.

Motivation: a deadsnakes PPA 503 failed a from-scratch ROCm base image build ([Buildkite #103973](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103973), `Ensure ROCm stack + runtime`).

## Claims

- A failed bake whose output shows `E: Failed to fetch <url> 408|429|500-504` exits 75 and is retried once (`refresh-rocm-base-amd` already retried 75; `image-build-amd` now does too, `limit: 1`).
- Any other bake failure (missing package, compile error, the vanished-`/tmp` AITER failure from #103973 attempt 1) still exits 1 immediately.

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/tools/test_rocm_build.py   # 59 passed
pre-commit run --files <changed>        # clean
```

- New `test_only_infrastructure_faults_retry_a_failed_stack_build`: the 503 case fails without the `build.sh` change and passes with it; the three recipe failures exit 1 either way.
- The classifier against real logs:

| Log | Failure | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| [#103973 attempt 2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/103973#01a1f04a-56c0-43a1-b6ec-598ef347b5d8) | `E: Failed to fetch .../python3.14_3.14.10-1+jammy1_amd64.deb 503 Service Unavailable` | 75 |
| #103973 attempt 1 | AITER prebuild: `lld: error: cannot open output file /tmp/...: No such file or directory` | 1 |
| #102331 | LMCache wheel check failure (a recipe bug, since fixed) | 1 |

## Details

- `ensure()` tees the bake output to a temp log and greps it only when the bake failed. Successful bakes are unaffected apart from the tee.
- The AITER `/tmp` ENOENT failure is deliberately not retried: it happened once, the same message is what a deterministic bug produces, and a retry repeats about 2.5 h of AITER prebuild. The root-cause notes are in #68527's description.
- Trade-off: the classifier matches log text, so a recipe bug that makes a mirror return 5xx gets one wasted retry (capped by `limit: 1`).
- Review history: njhill asked on #68527 to drop the vanished-file patterns (one occurrence, and a retry costs ~2.5 h); they were dropped there before the split, so `infra_failure` matches only apt fetch failures.
- Overlap: draft #68031 (latioswang) also adds an `exit_status: 75` rule to `image-build-amd`, for a different reason (base step still running, `limit: 4`). The two touch neighbouring lines; whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase, and the retry limits need reconciling. Not a duplicate: #68031 does not classify bake failures.

No other open PR changes `build.sh`'s failure classification (searched `build.sh exit 75 rocm`, `rocm image build retry mirror`).

This PR changes `build.sh`, so its own CI needs `/ci rocm nocache`.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Check the MLA W_UV kernel through a Triton launch hook
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`test_mla_v_up_proj_follows_tuned_aiter_triton_bf16_bmm` (added in #63397) fails intermittently on ROCm with an empty kernel list:

```text
>       assert ran_triton is tuned, kernels[True]
E       AssertionError: []
```

- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104469#01a1f664-a523-4aa3-9507-927c859a834c (MI300, `n1024-k4096-m100`)
- https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/104416#01a1f587-b06b-4c05-bd29-c08be234253c (MI355 DPX, `kimi-tp8-m64`)

The kernels run, but torch.profiler does not report them. On ROCm, rocprofiler-sdk writes the kernel dispatch record from its signal handler thread after the application already saw the kernel complete, and kineto ends the session with `rocprofiler_flush_buffer()` and `rocprofiler_stop_context()` without waiting for it. A short session like this one often ends before the record arrives. This is tracked in ROCm/rocm-systems#14378, and the fix is a new rocprofiler-sdk API in ROCm/rocm-systems#15046 (draft) that kineto would then call.

This records the launched Triton kernels with `triton.knobs.runtime.launch_enter_hook` instead, which Triton calls synchronously on every launch. The checks are unchanged.

## Claims

- The test no longer depends on torch.profiler delivering kernel records.
- It still fails when `_v_up_proj` does not run AITER's Triton BMM for a tuned shape, and still compares the output against the `torch.bmm` path.

## Validation

All runs use the CI image of the failing MI300 build (`rocm/vllm-ci:build-01a1f65f-da92-47ed-a604-e26662a505e7`) and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 pytest -q v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py -k test_mla_v_up_proj`.

| | MI300X | MI355X |
|---|---|---|
| main | fails in CI, see above | 17 of 100 runs fail |
| this PR | 100 of 100 runs pass | 100 of 100 runs pass |
| this PR, AITER path forced off in `_v_up_proj` | `m32` and `m100` fail with `AssertionError: []` | `m32`, `m100` and `kimi-tp8-m64` fail with `AssertionError: []` |

The profiler loss also shows up without vLLM or AITER. Profiling a single `torch.bmm` followed by `torch.accelerator.synchronize()`, 300 sessions each:

| Wait before the session ends | MI300X sessions with no GPU events | MI355X sessions with no GPU events |
|---|---|---|
| none | 99 | 29 |
| 0.1 ms | 0 | 0 |
| 1 ms | 0 | 0 |

With three kernels per session, some sessions also come back with only part of the records, so retrying an empty session would not be enough.

<details>
<summary>Profiler reproducer</summary>

```python
import time, torch
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity, DeviceType
a = torch.randn(4, 100, 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
b = torch.randn(4, 4096, 1024, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
for delay_ms in (0, 0.1, 1):
    blind = 0
    for _ in range(300):
        with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CUDA]) as prof:
            torch.bmm(a, b)
            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
            if delay_ms:
                time.sleep(delay_ms / 1000)
        if not any(e.device_type == DeviceType.CUDA for e in prof.events()):
            blind += 1
    print(f"delay={delay_ms}ms blind={blind}/300")
```

</details>

The launch hook saw `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel_...` on all 200 of 200 calls of `rocm_aiter_ops.triton_bf16_bmm`, and no AITER kernel on all 200 of 200 `torch.bmm` calls.

## Details

The hook sees only Triton launches, so the `use_triton=False` check now asserts that no AITER Triton BMM runs rather than that no such GPU kernel runs. commits.pr_title: [CI] Warm the Triton autotune cache in the MTP sharded-sampling test
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Add one warm-up boot to `test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence`, so the two compared boots run the same autotuned GDN kernels and the test checks only batch-sharded sampling. Fixes the flake in [AMD nightly 15860](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/15860). Related: #58342, #57026, #65733.

## Claims

**Sharding is not the cause.** Two boots with sharding disabled on both sides can diverge on the same prompts as the CI failure.

**The cause is per-rank Triton autotuning on a cold cache.** In the first boot each TP rank picks its own GDN kernel config; the second boot loads the one config left in the disk cache, so a rank can switch to a config that sums in a different order.

**The fix is test-only.** After the warm-up both compared boots load the same configs: 8 of 8 local runs had 0 divergent prompts. `MAX_DIVERGENT_PROMPTS` is unchanged.

## Validation

2x MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/vllm-ci:test-deps-rocm-aece323e26e87ef2` (torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, triton 3.8.0+git669b31ac), base `5a21c6c853` plus this change, empty Triton cache in every run (as in CI):

```bash
TRITON_CACHE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) TRITON_PRINT_AUTOTUNING=1 pytest -v -s \
    tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py::test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence
```

| Setup | Runs | Divergent prompts |
|---|---|---|
| main, CI build 15860 | 1 | greedy [16], seeded [12, 16, 17, 18]: failed |
| main, two boots both with sharding disabled (local print) | 8 | same as 15860 in 1 run, 0 in the rest |
| main, `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=0` (every boot autotunes) | 4 | greedy [16] in 3 runs, plus seeded [12, 16] in 2 |
| this PR | 8 | 0 in every run; autotuning only in the warm-up boot |

```
# this PR, MTP test only
1 passed, 26 warnings in 129.27s (0:02:09)
# this PR, whole file as CI runs it (MTP and DSpark)
2 passed, 32 warnings in 233.94s (0:03:53)
```

The MTP test takes about 20 s longer (129 to 147 s). CI already runs it in `Distributed DP Basic` on L4 and MI355; no config change is needed.

<details>
<summary>Failure on main (build 15860)</summary>

```
E       AssertionError: seeded: 4/20 prompts diverged at [12, 16, 17, 18], beyond near-tie noise
FAILED v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_sharded_sampling.py::test_mtp_sharded_sampling_equivalence
1 failed, 1 passed, 30 warnings in 207.98s (0:03:27)
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Qwen3.5 GDN prefill uses the Triton/FLA kernels, which have `@triton.autotune`, and vLLM caches autotune results on disk by default (#37188). Both TP ranks autotune in the first boot and write under the same key, so the second boot can run one rank on a different config. That moves logits in the low bits and flips near-tie tokens; with seeded sampling one flip changes the rest of the completion.

**Why this fix.** The warm-up takes the cold-cache step out of the comparison, so the compared boots differ only in sharding. #65733 fixed the same kind of flake in the DSpark test the same way: same kernels in both boots instead of a looser bound. The test sets `TRITON_CACHE_AUTOTUNING=1` because the warm-up only works through the disk cache.

**Why the bound stays at 3.** After #58342 made the check exact on Sep 24, it failed in 75 of 406 L4 runs on main on the same prompts, until #57026 raised the bound to 3 on Oct 15. L4 runs the same Triton/FLA path (confirmed in its CI log), so this fix likely covers it too, but I could not verify on L4. I plan to restore the exact check in a follow-up once CI shows 0 on both L4 and MI355.

**History.** The share of runs with any divergence rose from about 20% to about 50% on L4 after the Triton 3.8 update (#52183), and from under 1% to about 45% on MI355 after the ROCm 10 switch and image rework (#58761, #61939). Those updates are not bugs; they only changed how often the ranks pick different configs.

**Limitations.** Both TP ranks must share one `TRITON_CACHE_DIR`, which holds for this single-node test.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Support strided weights in sharded state saving
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`save_sharded_state` serializes each worker's in-memory `state_dict()`, i.e. the
weights *after* `process_weights_after_loading`. Some post-processing leaves a
weight as a non-contiguous view with a widened row stride. On ROCm,
`VLLM_ROCM_FP8_PADDING` (on by default) does exactly that with `F.pad(w, (0, n))[..., :-n]`.

Saving such a model fails twice over:

1. `ShardedStateLoader._filter_subtensors` computes a tensor's end address with
   `tensor.view(-1)[-1]`, which raises on a strided view:
   `RuntimeError: view size is not compatible with input tensor's size and stride`.
2. Even past that, `safetensors.save_file` refuses non-contiguous tensors:
   `ValueError: You are trying to save a non contiguous tensor`.

## Test plan

**1. FP8 model** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8`

```bash
python examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py \
    --model Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 --output /tmp/q3-fp8-sharded
```
- fails on main, passes here

Loading that FP8 checkpoint back is a separate, pre-existing problem: it fails
with `Missing keys (...attn.q_scale, ...k_scale, ...v_scale, ...prob_scale)`
on main too, even with `VLLM_ROCM_FP8_PADDING=0`, because those attention
scales are deleted in `process_weights_after_loading` and so never saved. It
is out of scope here.

**2. w4a16 model ** `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`:

```bash
python examples/features/sharded_state/save_sharded_state_offline.py \
    --model Qwen3-0.6B --output /tmp/q3-sharded
python examples/features/sharded_state/load_sharded_state_offline.py \
    --model /tmp/q3-sharded --load-format sharded_state \
    --prompt "The capital of France is" --max-tokens 32 --temperature 0
```
- fails on main, passes here

## Not a duplicate

No duplicate PRs found.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this PR. I reviewed every changed line, and ran the
tests and the end-to-end round trip listed above.
